document_title: CBD COP 9 Decision IX/16 C — Ocean Fertilization

document_title: CRCF Certification Methodologies — Future Permanent Removal Pathways
notes: The European Commission identifies ocean alkalinity enhancement as a possible future pathway for permanent carbon removal. The 2026 delegated rules currently cover only DACCS, BioCCS and biochar, and no EU certification methodology for OAE has yet been adopted.
source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action
status_note: Under methodology consideration; not yet certifiable under CRCF

document_title: CRCF Certification Methodologies — Future Permanent Removal Pathways
notes: The European Commission identifies direct capture from seawater followed by durable storage as a possible future permanent-removal pathway. No CRCF certification methodology for this approach had been adopted as of 2026.
source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action
status_note: Under methodology consideration; not yet certifiable under CRCF

document_title: Horizon Europe Call — The Ocean-Climate-Biodiversity Nexus and Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal
notes: The funding topic supports research on the biogeochemistry, ecology, health effects, public acceptance, governance, life-cycle performance and MRV of ocean alkalinity enhancement. It explicitly excludes field experiments.
source: European Commission, Horizon Europe / CORDIS
status_note: Published research call

document_title: Netherlands Carbon Dioxide Removal Roadmap
notes: The roadmap concludes that direct ocean capture could contribute to future carbon removal, describes electrochemical seawater decarbonization, low-to-medium technology readiness and Dutch SeaO2 and Brineworks demonstrations, and emphasizes that potential and costs remain highly uncertain.
source: Ministry of Climate Policy and Green Growth, Netherlands
status_note: Adopted national roadmap

document_title: Netherlands Carbon Dioxide Removal Roadmap
notes: The roadmap does not further pursue addition of alkaline materials or nutrient and iron fertilization because of low technology readiness and potentially substantial ecosystem risks, and it notes CBD restrictions on iron fertilization.
source: Ministry of Climate Policy and Green Growth, Netherlands
status_note: Screened but not prioritized for national deployment policy

document_title: Decree No. 12,045/2024 — National Programme for Conservation and Sustainable Use of Brazilian Mangroves (ProManguezal)
notes: A presidential decree formally established ProManguezal, integrating mangrove conservation, restoration and sustainable use into national governance. It expressly recognizes mangroves' role in climate mitigation, adaptation and carbon storage and calls for research on carbon stocks and sink accounting.
source: Presidency of the Republic of Brazil / Ministry of Environment and Climate Change
status_note: In force since 6 June 2024

document_title: Draft Decree Amending the General Law on Climate Change — Blue Carbon
notes: The proposed amendment would define blue carbon in the General Climate Change Law and require national climate policy to prioritize conservation and restoration of coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass beds. The Chamber of Deputies approved it in March 2026 and sent it to the Senate; it has not yet become law.
source: Chamber of Deputies of Mexico
status_note: Approved by Chamber of Deputies; pending Senate review

document_title: Mangrove Initiative for Shoreline Habitats & Tangible Incomes (MISHTI)
notes: India launched MISHTI in 2023 to coordinate mangrove afforestation and restoration across government programmes over five years. Official documents identify carbon sequestration, coastal protection and livelihood benefits as core outcomes.
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change / Press Information Bureau, India
status_note: Under implementation (five-year programme)

document_title: Chile Long-Term Climate Strategy 2050 — Ocean and Blue Carbon Targets
notes: The ocean chapter of the long-term climate strategy calls for a blue-carbon roadmap, financing for the national ocean plan and ocean-based nature solutions that protect carbon stocks and sink capacity in marine and coastal ecosystems, together with mitigation indicators for marine protected areas.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Chile
status_note: Adopted national long-term strategy

subnational_area: Five coastal wetlands in central-southern Chile
document_title: Study: Coastal Wetlands as Blue Carbon Sinks
notes: A GEF coastal-wetlands project led by the environment ministry measured sedimentary organic-carbon stocks in five wetlands and estimated emissions that could result from degradation, providing official evidence for prioritizing conservation, restoration, compensation and blue-carbon policy.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Chile / GEF Coastal Wetlands Project
status_note: Published government-supported assessment

document_title: Climate Change Act 2021 — Part 13 Oceans and Climate Change
notes: The Climate Change Act authorizes the minister to adopt regulations, policies and measures to protect blue-carbon reservoirs and advance science- and data-based conservation and restoration of marine and coastal ecosystems. It also provides a legal basis for carbon-right arrangements in blue-carbon projects.
source: Office of the Attorney-General, Fiji
status_note: In force

document_title: Updated Nationally Determined Contribution — Blue Carbon Commitments
notes: Seychelles' 2021 updated NDC strengthens the ocean–climate nexus and commits to protecting 100% of critical blue-carbon ecosystems, including seagrass beds and mangroves, as foundations for mitigation, coastal protection and fisheries productivity.
source: Ministry of Environment, Climate, Energy and Natural Resources, Seychelles
status_note: Submitted and active NDC

document_title: Panama Updated NDC — Blue Carbon Inventory and Mangrove Restoration Commitments
notes: The updated NDC requires estimation of national blue-carbon potential in the greenhouse-gas inventory from 2022 and proposes implementation of a technical manual for restoring degraded mangroves, treating coastal-wetland conservation and restoration as nature-based solutions under the Paris Agreement.
source: Ministry of Environment, Panama
status_note: Submitted and under implementation

document_title: Draft Policy Instrument: Blue Carbon in Mangroves
notes: Panama's environment ministry conducted public consultation in 2023 on a draft blue-carbon regulation for mangroves. The public page confirms the draft and comment form but does not show subsequent formal adoption, so the record remains classified as consultation.
source: Ministry of Environment, Panama
status_note: Public consultation completed; adoption not confirmed

document_title: NRC-IRAP Contribution — Tufts Cove OAE Pilot: Testing and Monitoring of MODOM
notes: Canada's National Research Council funded the Tufts Cove ocean-alkalinity trial to validate data on continuous carbon removal, life-cycle emissions accounting and the MODOM dosing and monitoring system.
source: National Research Council Canada — Industrial Research Assistance Program
status_note: Completed contribution agreement

document_title: NRC-IRAP Contribution — Scaling Carbon Removal at Tufts Cove
notes: Federal funding supports the design, construction and operation of a full-scale continuous OAE system capable of using multiple alkaline feedstocks. It is being designed using pilot data and for the largest scale likely to be permitted, with a target cost below USD 250 per tonne.
source: National Research Council Canada — Industrial Research Assistance Program
status_note: Active contribution agreement (2025–2026)

document_title: NRC-IRAP Contribution — Operational Cost Reduction for OAE Deployment
notes: The project seeks commercial validation of a calcium-based OAE dosing system, aims to reduce operating cost per tonne of removal by at least 60%, and targets delivery of 12,000 tonnes of verified carbon removal in 2026 to test reliability and community acceptance for commercial-scale deployment.
source: National Research Council Canada — Industrial Research Assistance Program
status_note: Active contribution agreement (2026–2027)

document_title: NRC-IRAP Contribution — Staged Leaching Research with Systematic Investigation
notes: Federal funding supports staged leaching research from laboratory to pilot scale to assess industrial by-products as OAE feedstocks and define process design, economics and major environmental and operational risks.
source: National Research Council Canada — Industrial Research Assistance Program
status_note: Active contribution agreement (2026–2028)

subnational_area: Red Sea and Arabian Gulf coasts
document_title: Saudi Green Initiative / NCVC Mangrove Planting Programme — 100 Million Mangrove Target
notes: Under the Saudi Green Initiative, the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification is restoring mangroves along the Red Sea and Arabian Gulf coasts and has announced a partnership target of planting 100 million mangroves, linked to climate action and coastal restoration.
source: National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification, Saudi Arabia
status_note: Under implementation

document_title: Climate Change Coastal Adaptation Response Plan
notes: The national coastal adaptation response plan places ecosystems at its core, explicitly prioritizes restoration and protection of blue- and green-carbon sinks, and advances more than 150 interventions through local implementation and climate-finance mechanisms.
source: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment, South Africa
status_note: Launched and under implementation

document_title: Carbon Markets Governance Framework — Blue Carbon Project Development
notes: The government announced development of a carbon-market governance framework and identified the blue-carbon potential of roughly 3,000 kilometres of coastline, restoration of mangroves, seagrass and salt marshes, and pilot-project development as marine and coastal opportunities. Detailed methodologies and project rules remain under development.
source: South African Government News Agency / Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment
status_note: Framework and pilot pipeline under development

document_title: Resolution No. 53/2024 — Blue Economy Development Strategy 2024–2033
notes: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 53/2024 approved the Blue Economy Development Strategy 2024–2033. Government blue-carbon materials state that the strategy includes specific actions to protect blue-carbon ecosystems and links them with investment and natural-resource governance.
source: Council of Ministers / National Press of Mozambique
status_note: Approved by Resolution No. 53/2024

document_title: Mozambique Blue Carbon Readiness Framework Assessment
notes: ProAzul and the World Bank's PROBLUE programme conducted a national blue-carbon readiness assessment and proposed a practical framework and strategic recommendations for scaling public and private investment across mangroves, seagrass and salt-marsh ecosystems.
source: Blue Economy Development Fund (ProAzul), Mozambique / World Bank PROBLUE
status_note: Assessment and pilot-readiness process completed

document_title: National Mangrove Ecosystem Management Plan 2017–2027
notes: Kenya's national mangrove ecosystem management plan establishes a framework for conservation, restoration, sustainable use, monitoring and community participation. Subsequent government research links the plan to mangrove blue-carbon potential and climate-mitigation value.
source: Kenya Forest Service
status_note: Adopted plan (2017–2027)

document_title: Viet Nam National Blue Carbon Action Partnership (NBCAP)
notes: In 2026, Viet Nam's Ministry of Agriculture and Environment formally launched the National Blue Carbon Action Partnership, established a steering committee by ministerial decision and designated UNDP to host the secretariat. The active platform coordinates knowledge, policy, finance and project preparation for ecosystems such as mangroves and seagrass; it does not itself issue carbon credits or create a uniform mandatory MRV standard.
source: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, Viet Nam
status_note: Officially launched in May 2026; Leadership Board and UNDP-hosted Secretariat are active

document_title: Mangrove Blue Carbon Roadmap to 2030 and Beyond — Science-Policy Process
notes: DOST-PCAARRD, DENR and partner institutions support development of a mangrove blue-carbon roadmap for 2030 and beyond covering science, governance, livelihood equity, conservation technologies, investment and finance, and shared data. Public information indicates that the roadmap remains under development.
source: Department of Science and Technology — PCAARRD, Philippines
status_note: Roadmap under development through a government-supported science-policy process

document_title: Senate Bill No. 1722 — Mangrove Forest Preservation Act
notes: The bill would establish and protect mangrove reserves and appropriate funding. Its direct purpose is mangrove conservation rather than stand-alone carbon-removal accounting, although it would protect important blue-carbon reservoirs. It remained under committee consideration as of February 2026.
source: Senate of the Philippines
status_note: Pending in committee as of 3 February 2026

document_title: Mangrove Accounts of the Philippines — Extent Accounts Technical Notes
notes: The Philippine Statistics Authority published technical notes for mangrove extent accounts, establishing a basis for national ecosystem accounting and recognizing mangroves as major blue-carbon sinks. The current account primarily measures area and is not yet a complete carbon-stock or carbon-sink methodology.
source: Philippine Statistics Authority
status_note: Published official technical accounting guidance

document_title: Federal Blue Carbon Policy, Guidelines and Credit Trading Platform Initiative
notes: Malaysia's federal government announced plans to develop a blue-carbon policy or guidance and explore a blue-carbon credit trading platform in coordination with Sabah institutions. Because formal rules and the platform remain under development, the record is classified as proposed policy.
source: Ministry of Finance, Malaysia (official press citation)
status_note: Announced; policy, guidelines and trading platform under development

document_title: Guidelines for Mangrove Restoration in the UAE
notes: The United Arab Emirates issued its first national technical guidance for mangrove restoration, providing locally adapted methods for project siting, planning and implementation and supporting the national roadmap to plant 100 million mangroves by 2030.
source: Environment Agency – Abu Dhabi / Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, UAE
status_note: Published national guidance

document_title: Marine Climate Change Science Programme — BlueCarbonSG
notes: The National Parks Board's Marine Climate Change Science programme funds BlueCarbonSG for 2023–2026 to account for, map and model carbon stocks and fluxes in mangroves, seagrass beds and mudflats and to develop a framework for potentially incorporating quantified blue-carbon targets into national greenhouse-gas reporting for the first time.
source: National Parks Board, Singapore
status_note: Funded research programme in progress (2023–2026)

document_title: Bangladesh’s Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0)
notes: NDC 3.0 incorporates mangrove restoration and coastal afforestation into national mitigation, adaptation and just-transition pathways. It calls for scaling restoration to protect coasts and enhance carbon storage and lists coastal afforestation as an AFOLU mitigation action.
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bangladesh / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Pakistan Nationally Determined Contribution 3.0
notes: NDC 3.0 calls for mangrove protection, wetland development and stronger coastal protection and ecological resilience. Its implementation matrix separately identifies mangrove restoration as an urban and coastal resilience measure.
source: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Pakistan / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Sri Lanka Nationally Determined Contributions 3.0 (2026–2035) — Blue Carbon NDC 4
notes: Blue Carbon NDC 4 requires restoration of 150 hectares of degraded mangroves annually from 2026 to 2035 and reduction of estimated mangrove-conversion losses of 0.5% per year. Mangrove planting is used to quantify the NDC's net-removal contribution.
source: Ministry of Environment, Sri Lanka / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC for 2026–2035

document_title: Sri Lanka Nationally Determined Contributions 3.0 (2026–2035) — Blue Carbon NDC 4
notes: Blue Carbon NDC 4 sets indicators for identifying, mapping, conserving and restoring seagrass beds. Because data are insufficient, it does not currently quantify removals, and this record is therefore separated from the quantified mangrove target.
source: Ministry of Environment, Sri Lanka / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC for 2026–2035; removal quantity not yet quantified

document_title: Sri Lanka Nationally Determined Contributions 3.0 (2026–2035) — Blue Carbon NDC 4
notes: Blue Carbon NDC 4 sets indicators for identifying, mapping, conserving and restoring salt marshes. It does not yet quantify salt-marsh removals, so the record is treated as a separate ecosystem pathway at the MRV-readiness stage.
source: Ministry of Environment, Sri Lanka / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC for 2026–2035; removal quantity not yet quantified

document_title: Programa Floresta Azul — Restauro Ecológico de Pradarias Marinhas
notes: The government approved EUR 2 million for the Blue Forests programme, covering seagrass mapping, ecological restoration and planting, nursery development and community participation. It also requires quantification of sequestration potential to support possible commercialization of voluntary-market credits.
source: Government of Portugal — Ministry of Environment and Energy; Ministry of Agriculture and Sea
status_note: Approved in December 2025; two-year implementation programme

subnational_area: Protected coastal, estuarine and lagoon areas
document_title: Floresta Azul Call No. 04/2026 — Ecological Restoration of Seagrass Meadows
notes: In 2026, the Environmental Fund opened a EUR 1 million funding window for mapping seagrass in protected areas, assessing ecological condition, monitoring and quantifying sequestration capacity, physical protection and restoration, and development of land-based or underwater nurseries.
source: Government of Portugal / Environmental Fund
status_note: Funding call opened in May 2026

document_title: Royal Decree on the Conservation of Marine Angiosperm Meadows in the Spanish Mediterranean
notes: The royal decree establishes a unified legal framework to protect Posidonia oceanica and Cymodocea nodosa seagrass beds, regulate vessel anchoring, promote low-impact moorings and support scientific monitoring and restoration of degraded areas. The official notice focuses on ecosystem protection and does not set a separate carbon-removal accounting target; it is included as protective regulation for a seagrass-based ONCE ecosystem.
source: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge, Spain
status_note: Approved by Council of Ministers on 10 March 2026

document_title: Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan — Saltmarsh Actions
notes: Scotland's first blue-carbon action plan treats salt marsh as a distinct action area. The government and NatureScot are deploying multi-year greenhouse-gas flux-tower monitoring and supporting evidence through the UK Blue Carbon Evidence Partnership for possible future inclusion of salt marshes in the UK greenhouse-gas inventory.
source: Scottish Government — Marine Directorate
status_note: Published September 2025; actions scheduled through 2028/29

document_title: Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan — Seagrass Actions
notes: The action plan identifies seagrass as a priority habitat capable of generating additional carbon uptake through restoration and enhancement. It provides for improved mapping, research on carbon stocks and sequestration rates, and assessment of how protection measures affect seagrass and its carbon stores.
source: Scottish Government — Marine Directorate
status_note: Published September 2025; actions scheduled through 2028/29

document_title: Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan — Seabed Sediment Actions
notes: The plan treats seabed sediments as an emerging blue-carbon habitat and calls for local research to be expanded into a Scotland-wide sediment-carbon assessment in 2026/27–2027/28, including analysis of disturbance risks and the protective effect of existing or proposed fisheries-management measures.
source: Scottish Government — Marine Directorate
status_note: Evidence actions underway or scheduled through 2028/29

document_title: Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan — Kelp and Other Seaweeds Actions
notes: The plan treats kelp and other macroalgae as a separate emerging blue-carbon pathway. It recognizes CO2 uptake through photosynthesis but notes that long-term storage depends on detritus reaching and being buried in seabed sediments; actions focus on systematic review, carbon fate and life-cycle evidence rather than direct credit issuance.
source: Scottish Government — Marine Directorate
status_note: Evidence-development actions scheduled through 2028/29

document_title: Oman Blue Carbon Project — Contract to Plant 100 Million Mangrove Trees
notes: The Environment Authority contracted Oman's first mangrove-based blue-carbon credit project, planning to plant 100 million mangroves over four years across approximately 20,000 hectares in Al Wusta, including artificial-lagoon areas. Official estimates suggest approximately 14 million tonnes of CO2 could be reduced or removed and monetized as blue-carbon credits.
source: Environment Authority, Sultanate of Oman / Oman News Agency
status_note: Implementation contract signed 16 October 2023

document_title: National Afforestation Plan 2022–2035 — Mangrove Expansion Target
notes: The Cabinet-approved national afforestation plan calls for quadrupling the number of mangroves by 2035 and links this objective to the country's 2035 emissions commitment and 2060 carbon-neutrality target. The plan includes government projects, public participation, supporting policies, common standards and progress monitoring.
source: Ministry of Municipalities Affairs and Agriculture, Bahrain
status_note: Cabinet-approved national plan for 2022–2035

document_title: National Afforestation Plan Implementation Update — Bahrain Mangroves Initiative
notes: An official progress update in December 2025 reported that Bahrain's mangrove initiative had planted approximately 2.2 million seedlings, reaching 138% of the original interim 2035 target of 1.6 million. This record documents implementation progress and is kept separate from the 2022–2035 target record.
source: Government of Bahrain — SDGs Bahrain
status_note: Official implementation update published 25 December 2025

document_title: Belize Updated NDC Commitment — Mangrove Carbon Sink
notes: Belize commits to increasing the carbon-sink capacity of mangrove and seagrass ecosystems by 2030 and to removing a cumulative 381,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent through mangrove restoration during 2021–2030, while strengthening mangrove protection.
source: Forest Department of Belize
status_note: Active NDC commitment through 2030

document_title: Belize Updated NDC Commitment — Seagrass Carbon Sink
notes: The same national commitment specifically calls for increasing seagrass carbon-sink capacity by 2030. The official page does not assign a separate quantified removal value to seagrass, so it is recorded separately from the 381,000-tonne mangrove-restoration target.
source: Forest Department of Belize
status_note: Active NDC commitment through 2030; seagrass removal quantity not separately specified

document_title: The Bahamas NDC 3.0 — Mangrove and Coastal Ecosystem Restoration
notes: NDC 3.0 calls for a national blue-carbon programme to enhance greenhouse-gas sink capacity and reports that 50 hectares of mangroves are under active restoration, supported by site-management plans and community monitoring. It also identifies mangrove conservation and restoration as actions to improve carbon storage and coastal resilience.
source: Office of the Prime Minister, The Bahamas / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in 2025; restoration activities ongoing

document_title: The Bahamas NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Carbon Storage and Blue-Carbon Markets
notes: NDC 3.0 states that The Bahamas contains one of the world's largest seagrass systems and that it is important for global carbon storage and sequestration. The policy matrix calls for a national blue-carbon programme and identifies blue-carbon markets for mangrove and seagrass conservation as a future financing opportunity.
source: Office of the Prime Minister, The Bahamas / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in 2025; programme and market development planned

document_title: National Action Plan for Ecosystem Services Accounting and Natural Capital Valuation
notes: The Cabinet approved a national action plan for ecosystem-service accounting and natural-capital valuation in September 2023, establishing standardized measurement and monetary-valuation frameworks for natural assets. The second NDC states that carbon-accounting methods for marine systems such as seagrass must be developed and that coastal authorities are working toward inclusion in national accounts.
source: Government of Barbados / Coastal Zone Management Unit
status_note: Cabinet-approved in September 2023; integration work ongoing

document_title: Barbados Second Nationally Determined Contribution — Mangrove Protection
notes: The second NDC commits to implementing the 2020 Water Resources Protection and Land Use Policy to protect mangroves and other coastal ecosystems and confirms continued mangrove protection as a land-use and forestry action. It provides no separate removal estimate.
source: Government of Barbados / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC submitted in August 2025

document_title: Barbados Second Nationally Determined Contribution — Seagrass Protection
notes: The second NDC commits to protecting seagrass beds through the 2020 Water Resources Protection and Land Use Policy and notes the need for internationally consistent seagrass carbon-accounting methods. Because protection and accounting-readiness measures occur together, this record is kept separate from the mangrove entry.
source: Government of Barbados / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC submitted in August 2025

document_title: Dominican Republic NDC 3.0 — Zero Net Mangrove Loss in Protected Areas by 2030
notes: NDC 3.0 targets zero net loss of mangroves in protected areas by 2030, with an estimated 660,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent absorbed or avoided. Planning covers 2025–2030 and implementation 2026–2030, using the IPCC Wetlands Supplement and UNFCCC methods for MRV and mobilizing blue-carbon and forest-carbon finance.
source: Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources / National Council for Climate Change and Carbon Market, Dominican Republic
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; implementation scheduled for 2026–2030

document_title: Senegal First Nationally Determined Contribution — Mangrove Reforestation and Restoration
notes: Senegal's NDC calls for approximately 1,297 hectares of mangrove afforestation or restoration each year, rising to 4,000 hectares annually under the conditional enhanced scenario. Implementation may be supported by carbon-market mechanisms that comply with Paris Agreement Article 6 requirements for environmental integrity and avoidance of double counting.
source: Government of Senegal / UNFCCC
status_note: Active first NDC submitted in December 2020

document_title: Cuba NDC 3.0 — Blue Carbon Removal Potential Assessment Priority
notes: Cuba's NDC 3.0 identifies assessment of blue-carbon potential as an important requirement and priority for identifying additional atmospheric CO2-removal potential. It also notes mitigation co-benefits from coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, but the ecosystem scope, accounting methods and removal targets remain under study, so the record is not forced into a single pathway.
source: Government of Cuba / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in February 2025; technology and target definition under study

document_title: Label bas-carbone Method — Posidonia Seagrass Meadows
notes: France's national Low-Carbon Label methodology accounts for carbon benefits from preventing anchoring-related degradation of Mediterranean Posidonia seagrass beds. Eligible activities include no-anchor zones, low-impact mooring areas and their management and maintenance. The project period is ten years and may be renewed twice, with reductions verified ex post. The pathway primarily protects existing sediment carbon and avoids remineralization emissions rather than comprehensively accounting for additional seagrass growth.
source: French Ministry for Ecological Transition — Label bas-carbone
status_note: Government-approved methodology in force

document_title: Label bas-carbone Method — Restoration of Mangroves and Swamp Forests
notes: This national Low-Carbon Label methodology was approved on 30 November 2023 and applies to degraded mangroves or swamp forests with less than 60% canopy cover. It allows both passive restoration, such as improving tidal hydrology, and active planting, and accounts separately for above-ground, below-ground and soil carbon pools. The ten-year project period may be renewed twice and includes discounts for non-permanence and data uncertainty.
source: French Ministry for Ecological Transition — Label bas-carbone
status_note: Approved national methodology in force since November 2023

document_title: Marine Institute Blue Carbon Research Investment — Saltmarsh Workstream
notes: Ireland's Marine Institute invested EUR 2.6 million through its 2021 Blue Carbon call, funding two research teams to study national marine blue carbon. Official materials identify salt marsh as one of Ireland's two confirmed blue-carbon habitats; this record covers only the salt-marsh research pathway so it can be screened separately from seagrass and seabed sediment carbon.
source: Marine Institute, Ireland
status_note: Publicly funded multi-year research programme announced in February 2022

document_title: Marine Institute Blue Carbon Research Investment — Seagrass Workstream
notes: The same EUR 2.6 million national research investment expressly identifies seagrass beds as Irish blue-carbon habitats. This record focuses on evidence concerning seagrass carbon stocks, cycling and management and is kept separate from salt marshes and seabed sediments.
source: Marine Institute, Ireland
status_note: Publicly funded multi-year research programme announced in February 2022

document_title: Marine Institute Blue Carbon Research Investment — Seabed Sediment Workstream
notes: Ireland's official research investment also examines potential blue-carbon systems across extensive marine areas, particularly sediment carbon stores, seabed physical processes, long-term carbon cycling and high-quality spatial mapping. This is an assessment and protection pathway for seabed sediment carbon, not active engineered removal.
source: Marine Institute, Ireland
status_note: Publicly funded multi-year research programme announced in February 2022

subnational_area: Ireland, Canada, Germany, Malta, Norway, Poland and Greece
document_title: JPI Oceans Joint Call on Blue Carbon Ecosystems 2025
notes: Funding agencies from seven countries pooled approximately EUR 5.3 million for research on carbon stocks and fluxes in blue-carbon ecosystems, vulnerability to climate and human pressures, and the effectiveness and scalability of restoration and protection measures. The call did not prescribe a single habitat, so the pathway is to be determined by individual funded projects rather than being forced into mangrove or seagrass categories.
source: JPI Oceans / Marine Institute and participating national funders
status_note: Joint call launched in 2025; proposal deadline was 2 March 2026

document_title: Guyana Nationally Determined Contributions 2025–2035
notes: Guyana's NDC proposes expanding mangrove restoration and protecting mangrove ecosystems along vulnerable coastlines and riverbanks. Its adaptation chapter again identifies mangrove restoration and ecosystem protection as actions to be implemented subject to adequate finance, including carbon-market funding. It provides no separate quantified mangrove-removal estimate.
source: Government of Guyana / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted on 1 July 2026; restoration scale conditional on finance

document_title: Mauritius NDC 3.0 — Ocean Carbon Sink and Seagrass Targets
notes: Mauritius' NDC explicitly treats the ocean as a carbon sink and calls for nursery-based seagrass restoration, a combined 5% increase in mangrove and seagrass cover, nationwide mapping and carbon inventories by 2027, inclusion of blue-carbon stocks in the national greenhouse-gas inventory and climate reporting by 2030, and full operationalization by 2035. This record separately captures the seagrass pathway.
source: Government of Mauritius / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Mauritius NDC 3.0 — Ocean Carbon Sink and Mangrove Targets
notes: The NDC calls for marine protected areas in high-carbon mangrove zones, a combined 5% increase in mangrove and seagrass cover, mapping and carbon inventories, and inclusion in national greenhouse-gas reporting. It also targets an increase in Rodrigues mangroves from roughly 30 hectares to 50 hectares by 2030. This record is separated from the seagrass restoration target.
source: Government of Mauritius / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Jamaica NDC 3.0 — Mangrove and Forested-Wetland Targets
notes: Jamaica's NDC proposes restoring at least 2,200 hectares of mangroves by 2030 and a further 1,000 hectares of converted or degraded forested wetlands by 2035. It also plans to include mangroves in the national greenhouse-gas inventory by 2030 and establish a no-net-loss policy for coastal wetlands by 2035. Restoration is unconditional, while inventory integration and no-net-loss policy are conditional actions.
source: Government of Jamaica / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Jamaica NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Carbon-Stock Mapping and Protection
notes: The NDC requires mapping and carbon-stock assessment of Jamaica's nearshore seagrass ecosystems by 2030 and further assessment of seagrass extent in the exclusive economic zone. By 2035 it aims to protect all seagrass ecosystems within gazetted protected areas. Nearshore mapping and carbon assessment are unconditional; EEZ assessment and comprehensive protection are conditional.
source: Government of Jamaica / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Solomon Islands NDC 3.0 — New Sustainable Mangrove Forest Target
notes: Solomon Islands' NDC 3.0 sets an activity indicator of 4,000 additional hectares of sustainably managed mangroves by 2035. The area is listed separately from terrestrial forest expansion and forms part of the national mitigation and resilience package. No separate CO2-removal estimate is provided, so the database retains the area target without converting it into carbon.
source: Government of Solomon Islands / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in 2025; implementation dependent on national and international support

document_title: Cambodia NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Restoration and Management Target
notes: Cambodia's NDC aquatic-habitat action table uses a 20,398-hectare mangrove baseline and targets restoration of 6,120 hectares, or 30%, by 2035. A separate FOLU measure seeks improved management, governance and restoration of 4,080 hectares of mangroves by 2035 and expressly includes enhanced sequestration benefits. Because the two measures may overlap, their areas are not added together.
source: Royal Government of Cambodia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in August 2025

document_title: Cambodia NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Restoration Target
notes: The NDC aquatic-habitat action table targets restoration of 4,167 hectares of seagrass, or 30%, by 2035, supported by GIS, vessel monitoring, drones and citizen science. The action is primarily framed around adaptation and fisheries resilience and provides no separate seagrass-removal estimate, so it is recorded as a blue-carbon-related restoration target rather than an accounted negative-emissions measure.
source: Royal Government of Cambodia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in August 2025

document_title: DMCR Qualifications and Criteria for Registered Mangrove-Planting Operators for Carbon-Credit Benefits, B.E. 2567
notes: Thailand's Department of Marine and Coastal Resources issued eligibility and registration criteria for participating operators under 2024 rules governing allocation of carbon credits from mangrove planting and maintenance. The system is intended to support greenhouse-gas mitigation, low-carbon growth and multi-stakeholder participation; this record concerns access rules for mangrove crediting rather than a single project.
source: Department of Marine and Coastal Resources, Thailand
status_note: Official criteria issued under the B.E. 2567 carbon-credit sharing regulation; published online in April 2025

document_title: Salak Jai @ Salak Khok Blue Carbon Mangrove Credit Pilot MOU
notes: In July 2026, Thailand's Department of Marine and Coastal Resources, CP All and the Ban Salak Khok community signed a pilot memorandum to restore degraded areas, expand natural mangrove sinks and develop the project to Thailand's T-VER standard, using carbon credits to support community income. This is project-level market preparation and does not mean national credits have already been issued.
source: Department of Marine and Coastal Resources, Thailand
status_note: Pilot MOU signed in July 2026; T-VER project development planned

subnational_area: Degraded mangrove forests and associated coastal wetlands
document_title: Suriname NDC 3.0 — Mangrove and Coastal-Wetland Restoration Target
notes: Suriname's NDC 3.0 proposes active, nature-based restoration of at least 5,000 hectares of degraded mangroves and associated coastal wetlands. The indicator is framed mainly around ecosystem restoration and resilience and does not separately quantify CO2 removals, so no carbon value is inferred.
source: Government of Suriname / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in November 2025

subnational_area: South East Coast, Mandele Point to Laborie
document_title: Government Blue Carbon Assessment Consultancy — Mangrove Workstream
notes: Saint Lucia procured consulting services to establish a blue-carbon baseline and monitoring and reporting tools for marine-ecosystem restoration on the southeast coast. Tasks include accounting for carbon benefits from mangrove restoration, applying methods such as GEF Blue Forests, assessing sites for community-based blue-carbon offset projects and integrating blue-carbon value into national ecosystem-management policy.
source: Government of Saint Lucia — Department of Sustainable Development
status_note: Government-funded consultancy tender issued in June 2022

subnational_area: South East Coast, Mandele Point to Laborie
document_title: Government Blue Carbon Assessment Consultancy — Seagrass Workstream
notes: The same government consultancy requires a baseline for the spatial extent and carbon accounting of seagrass beds, estimation of carbon benefits from proposed seagrass and other coastal restoration, development of systematic monitoring and reporting protocols, and assessment of potential sites for community-based seagrass offsets. This record is separated from the mangrove workstream.
source: Government of Saint Lucia — Department of Sustainable Development
status_note: Government-funded consultancy tender issued in June 2022

subnational_area: EU Member States and LIFE-associated countries
document_title: LIFE-2026-SAP-CLIMA-CCM — Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Priority
notes: The EU LIFE 2026 climate-mitigation call specifically encourages ocean alkalinity enhancement projects and supports innovative technology testing, carbon-flux measurement and verification capacity, and business-model development. The open funding call does not constitute EU deployment authorization or CRCF certification for OAE.
source: European Commission / LIFE Programme / CINEA
status_note: Open call published 21 April 2026; deadline 22 September 2026

subnational_area: EU Member States and LIFE-associated countries
document_title: LIFE-2026-SAP-CLIMA-CCM — Direct Ocean Capture Priority
notes: The same LIFE 2026 climate-mitigation call specifically encourages direct ocean capture as a permanent carbon-removal technology and supports technology validation, carbon-flux MRV capacity and business models. This funding opportunity does not replace permits for seawater abstraction and discharge, CO2 transport or durable storage.
source: European Commission / LIFE Programme / CINEA
status_note: Open call published 21 April 2026; deadline 22 September 2026

document_title: EU CRCF Methodology Support — Review of Carbon Removal by Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement
notes: The European Commission published a technical assessment of OAE for possible future permanent-removal methodologies under the CRCF. It recognizes storage of CO2 as dissolved inorganic carbon through ocean carbonate chemistry but identifies large-scale attribution, model-based accounting, ecological side effects and field-monitoring requirements as major certification challenges. It is not an adopted methodology.
source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action / Publications Office of the EU
status_note: Technical review released 18 March 2026; certification methodology not adopted

document_title: EU CRCF Methodology Support — Review of Direct Ocean Carbon Capture and Storage
notes: The European Commission's 2026 certification-methodology page lists an assessment of direct ocean capture and storage and identifies DOC with durable storage as a future permanent-removal pathway under exploration. Formal CRCF methods currently cover only DACCS, BioCCS and biochar, so DOC cannot yet be certified under an EU methodology.
source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action
status_note: Technical review listed in June 2026; certification methodology not adopted

document_title: HORIZON-MISS-2026-03-OCEAN-03 — Blue-Carbon Habitat Restoration Capacity
notes: The 2026 Restore our Ocean and Waters mission call requires projects to achieve measurable improvement in key marine habitats, including blue-carbon sequestration capacity, through active or passive protection and restoration, with demonstrations and sustained monitoring at five sites in at least three countries. Because the call does not prescribe mangroves, seagrass or salt marshes, the specific pathway is left to individual projects.
source: European Commission, Horizon Europe Mission Restore our Ocean and Waters
status_note: Open call published 4 February 2026; deadline 23 September 2026

subnational_area: Netherlands pilot with EU BlueInvest support
document_title: BlueInvest Readiness Assistance — SeaO2 Direct Ocean Capture Scale-up
notes: EU BlueInvest provided the Dutch company SeaO2 with investor engagement, strategic-planning and financing-readiness support. Its electrochemical DOC system treats seawater and returns low-CO2 water, enabling renewed atmospheric uptake; the Project Swell demonstration has a capacity of 25 tonnes of CO2 per year and prepares for future commercial credit delivery. The support does not mean the EU has approved a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission, Directorate-General for Maritime Affairs and Fisheries / BlueInvest
status_note: Readiness assistance delivered; pilot operating and commercial scale-up under preparation

subnational_area: Tuscany, Lazio, Campania, Sicily and Calabria
document_title: PNRR Marine Ecosystem Restoration (MER) — Posidonia Oceanica Restoration
notes: Italy's recovery and resilience plan allocated EUR 400 million to the 2022–2026 MER programme. It restores Posidonia seagrass beds in five coastal regions and adds protection measures to recover ecosystem services, biodiversity and carbon-sequestration capacity. The official page provides no separate CO2-removal estimate for this component.
source: Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security / ISPRA
status_note: National PNRR programme under implementation, 2022–2026

subnational_area: Tuscany, Lazio, Campania, Sicily and Calabria
document_title: PNRR Marine Ecosystem Restoration (MER) — Cystoseira Forest Restoration
notes: The MER programme includes restoration of Cystoseira brown-algal forests alongside seagrass and other sensitive habitats and identifies recovery of ecosystem services, biodiversity and carbon sequestration as overall objectives. This record separately identifies the macroalgal-forest pathway; the documents do not establish a long-term storage fraction or pathway-specific carbon amount.
source: Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security / ISPRA
status_note: National PNRR programme under implementation, 2022–2026

subnational_area: Marine protected areas, coastal national parks and Natura 2000 sites
document_title: PNRR Marine Ecosystem Restoration (MER) — Sustainable Mooring Fields
notes: MER is establishing 91 mooring areas with roughly 1,500 buoys to reduce or eliminate anchoring damage to seabeds and high-value coastal habitats. This is passive restoration and protection of existing carbon stocks. Avoided releases are not separately quantified, so the measure is not treated as quantified additional removal.
source: Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security / ISPRA
status_note: National installation programme under implementation

document_title: PNRR Marine Ecosystem Restoration (MER) — National Posidonia and Coastal-Habitat Mapping
notes: Under MER, Italy is updating a national Posidonia distribution map that had become outdated after more than twenty years, using satellites, airborne LiDAR, hyperspectral imagery, multibeam sonar and autonomous underwater vehicles within a common observation period. The work creates a spatial baseline for seagrass protection and potential blue-carbon accounting but is not presented as a national greenhouse-gas inventory method.
source: Italian Ministry of Environment and Energy Security / ISPRA
status_note: National mapping work under implementation through June 2026

document_title: LIFE SeaForest — Posidonia CO2 Sequestration Quantification Protocol
notes: LIFE SeaForest developed a methodological protocol for quantifying CO2 uptake and fixation by Posidonia and a replicable management tool to integrate blue-carbon value into climate policy and coastal planning. It is a project output and basis for future economic valuation, not yet an official Italian carbon-credit methodology.
source: ISPRA / LIFE SeaForest consortium
status_note: Methodological protocol published at project completion in 2025

subnational_area: Asinara, Santa Maria di Castellabate and La Maddalena protected areas
document_title: LIFE SeaForest — Posidonia Restoration and Avoided Anchoring Emissions
notes: The project restored more than 100 small degraded Posidonia sites, planted over 1,300 cuttings and installed sustainable mooring systems. An ISPRA report estimates that reducing uncontrolled anchoring degradation could avoid more than 5,365 tonnes of CO2 emissions over ten years. This mainly represents avoided loss of existing carbon stores rather than wholly additional removal.
source: ISPRA / LIFE SeaForest consortium
status_note: Demonstration project completed in December 2025

document_title: Neptune — Restoring Our Posidonia Oceanica Seagrass Meadows
notes: A Maltese government notice documents the country's first marine reforestation pilot: approximately 2,400 naturally detached Posidonia shoots were transplanted over 200 square metres of seabed in the Qawra Natura 2000 area, within a trial area of about one hectare. The project restores seagrass damaged by vessel activity but the notice does not quantify removals or avoided emissions.
source: Ministry for the Environment, Energy and Public Cleanliness, Malta / project partners
status_note: Pilot restoration underway; government-reported progress in May 2025

subnational_area: Region of Crete — Sitia, Aftzikari Bay
document_title: Interreg Euro-MED ARTEMIS — Crete Posidonia Restoration and Policy Integration
notes: The Region of Crete participates in the ARTEMIS project to improve Posidonia restoration techniques, evaluate ecosystem services and integrate findings into policy and investment decisions, with Aftzikari Bay near Sitia serving as a pilot restoration site. Official materials provide no separate removal estimate, so the record reflects technology and governance readiness.
source: Region of Crete / Interreg Euro-MED ARTEMIS partners
status_note: Regional pilot and policy-development project in progress in 2025

document_title: Samoa NDC 3.0 — 5% Mangrove Forest Area Expansion by 2035
notes: Samoa's NDC 3.0 sets an ocean-sector target to increase national mangrove area by 5% relative to 2022 by 2035. The document states that these adaptation targets are also expected to contribute to mitigation but provides no stand-alone CO2-removal accounting.
source: Government of Samoa / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in January 2026

document_title: Revised NDC 2.0 — Ocean Initiative Mangrove Restoration
notes: The revised NDC calls for advancing the national ocean initiative by 2030 through mangrove restoration, improved ocean governance and healthier seascapes and explicitly identifies both adaptation and mitigation benefits. It sets no mangrove-area or CO2-removal target, so none is inferred.
source: Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines / UNFCCC
status_note: Active revised NDC 2.0 submitted in 2025

document_title: Angola Nationally Determined Contribution 2025 — Mangrove Conservation and Blue-Carbon Co-benefits
notes: Angola's 2025 NDC includes protection of mangroves in provinces such as Zaire, Luanda and Benguela within coastal-ecosystem management. The measure is primarily framed as adaptation but expressly recognizes blue-carbon mitigation co-benefits; it sets no area or CO2-removal target.
source: Government of Angola / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC submitted in September 2025

document_title: Papua New Guinea Second NDC — Mangrove Mapping, Carbon Modelling and Inventory Integration
notes: Papua New Guinea's second NDC implementation arrangements call for mangrove mapping, carbon-stock modelling and reporting and for mangroves to be incorporated into the national greenhouse-gas inventory and biennial update reporting. This record captures the policy objective and MRV preparation; completion of inventory integration was not independently verified.
source: Climate Change and Development Authority, Papua New Guinea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC commitment; implementation completion not independently verified

document_title: Papua New Guinea Second NDC — Seagrass Blue-Carbon Policy and Data Pathway
notes: The same NDC calls for research on how mangroves and seagrass beds should be reflected in climate policy and for capacity in blue-carbon estimation, data collection, mapping, modelling, reporting and policy development. The seagrass pathway is recorded separately from mangrove inventory work, and no seagrass-removal quantity is given.
source: Climate Change and Development Authority, Papua New Guinea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC commitment; policy and inventory preparation stage

document_title: Mexico NDC 3.0 — National Blue Carbon Strategy, MRV and Market Governance
notes: Mexico's NDC 3.0 calls for the design and implementation of a national blue-carbon strategy, stronger methods for measuring carbon in marine and coastal ecosystems, and improved governance for access to voluntary markets and offset projects subject to environmental and social safeguards. This is a cross-ecosystem governance record; ecosystem-specific mangrove, seagrass and salt-marsh actions are recorded separately.
source: Government of Mexico / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in 2025

document_title: Mexico NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Conservation, Restoration and Carbon-Stock Enhancement
notes: NDC 3.0 calls for designing, implementing, monitoring and evaluating projects for mangrove conservation, restoration and sustainable management and for increasing carbon stocks and creating new sinks through the national blue-carbon strategy. It provides no separate area or removal amount for this measure.
source: Government of Mexico / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in 2025

document_title: Mexico NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Conservation and Restoration
notes: Mexico's NDC 3.0 identifies seagrass beds as blue-carbon ecosystems requiring projects for conservation, restoration and sustainable management, with monitoring and evaluation. The target recognizes their contribution to blue-carbon reservoirs but does not quantify additional removals.
source: Government of Mexico / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in 2025

document_title: Mexico NDC 3.0 — Salt-Marsh Conservation and Restoration
notes: NDC 3.0 expressly includes salt marshes in projects for conservation, restoration and sustainable management of marine and coastal ecosystems and requires monitoring and evaluation. This record is separated from mangroves and seagrass to identify the specific pathway; no salt-marsh removal quantity is given.
source: Government of Mexico / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in 2025

document_title: Palau NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Protection, Mapping and Restoration
notes: Palau's NDC 3.0 calls for updating sustainable forest-management policy to cover mangroves and wetlands, identifying and mapping resilient ecosystems, implementing protection measures and researching restoration. It expressly notes that mangroves capture carbon but sets no separate removal amount.
source: Government of Palau / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 29 January 2026

subnational_area: Palau National Marine Sanctuary and Blue Prosperity Plan areas
document_title: Palau NDC 3.0 — Marine Sanctuary and Blue Prosperity Plan for Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: The NDC calls for using the Palau National Marine Sanctuary and Blue Prosperity Plan to monitor pelagic fish and support ocean carbon storage through sustainable fisheries management. It does not specify whether storage occurs in seagrass, sediments, biomass or another pathway, so the technology is marked as unspecified and broad ocean-carbon estimates are not treated as formal removal targets.
source: Government of Palau / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 29 January 2026

document_title: Ghana Proposed Blue Economy Strategic Framework — Mangrove Blue-Carbon Protection
notes: A proposed strategic framework released by Ghana's Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development identifies mangroves as blue-carbon ecosystems requiring protection and proposes translating the framework into an updated blue-economy action plan backed by finance and performance indicators. The Cabinet memorandum was still under review, so it is classified as proposed policy.
source: Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development, Ghana
status_note: Proposed framework announced in May 2025; Cabinet memorandum under review

document_title: Ghana Proposed Blue Economy Strategic Framework — Tidal-Marsh Blue-Carbon Protection
notes: The same proposed framework identifies tidal salt marshes as blue-carbon ecosystems requiring protection. Because the policy was still under Cabinet review and set no salt-marsh area or carbon target, this pathway is recorded separately with proposed status.
source: Ministry of Fisheries and Aquaculture Development, Ghana
status_note: Proposed framework announced in May 2025; Cabinet memorandum under review

document_title: Nigeria Marine and Blue Economy Policy and National Carbon-Market Finance for Blue Carbon Projects
notes: Nigeria's Presidency states that a marine and blue-economy policy has been launched and that finance will be mobilized through the national carbon-market framework and Climate Change Fund for community-led blue-carbon projects. It also calls for blue-carbon markets under Paris Agreement Article 6. The statement specifies no methodology for mangroves, seagrass or salt marshes, so the pathway remains unspecified.
source: Office of the Vice President / State House, Nigeria
status_note: Marine and Blue Economy Policy reported as launched in November 2025; project methodologies not specified

document_title: Ogoniland and the Niger Delta: Mangrove Restoration and Conservation Strategy
notes: Nigeria's Federal Ministry of Environment, through HYPREP, issued a mangrove restoration and conservation strategy, restoration manual and field guidance and is implementing restoration in oil-polluted Ogoniland and the Niger Delta. Official notices do not quantify blue carbon or CO2 removal, so the record identifies ecosystem restoration with unquantified carbon benefits.
source: Federal Ministry of Environment, Nigeria / Hydrocarbon Pollution Remediation Project
status_note: Strategy and technical guidance unveiled in 2024; restoration implementation ongoing

document_title: Tuvalu NDC 3.0 — Nearshore Ocean-Based Carbon Sequestration Priority
notes: Tuvalu's NDC 3.0 proposes initiating ocean-carbon-sequestration activities focused on blue carbon in nearshore ecosystems and lists marine sequestration potential and opportunities as a conditional, medium-priority action. It does not identify mangroves, seagrass, salt marshes or another pathway and provides no removal estimate, so the pathway is marked unspecified and preparatory.
source: Government of Tuvalu / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in September 2025; conditional on finance, capacity and technology

subnational_area: Community mangrove sites in the Maldives
document_title: EU–Maldives Financing Agreement — Community-Based Mangrove Protection and Regeneration
notes: In 2026, the Government of Maldives and the European Union signed a financing agreement for community mangrove conservation and regeneration, providing implementation funding for protection, restoration and community participation. The official announcement emphasizes climate resilience and environmental protection and provides no separate CO2-removal estimate.
source: Government of Maldives / European Union
status_note: Financing agreement signed and announced on 21 May 2026

document_title: Maldives Blue Carbon Finance Capacity-Building Programme — Mangrove Workstream
notes: The Maldives Ministry of Tourism and Environment, Ministry of Finance and Planning, the United Nations and ESCAP launched capacity building on blue-carbon finance, including blended finance, public–private partnerships and results-based payments. This record covers only mangroves; the same activity also mentions seagrass and coral reefs, with seagrass recorded separately and coral reefs not treated as a carbon-removal pathway in this database.
source: Government of Maldives / United Nations / UN ESCAP
status_note: Capacity-building programme launched on 11 May 2025

document_title: Maldives Blue Carbon Finance Capacity-Building Programme — Seagrass Workstream
notes: The same blue-carbon-finance capacity-building initiative identifies seagrass beds as ecosystems that may support climate action and sustainable finance. This record separately captures financing and mechanism preparation for seagrass projects; the official announcement creates neither a seagrass carbon-accounting methodology nor a quantified removal target.
source: Government of Maldives / United Nations / UN ESCAP
status_note: Capacity-building programme launched on 11 May 2025

document_title: National Mangrove Management and Development Strategy 2025–2035
notes: The Tanzania Forest Services Agency published a ten-year national mangrove management and development strategy in 2025, providing a national framework for conservation, restoration and sustainable use. Government communications also place mangrove carbon trading and livelihood value on the implementation agenda, while project-level rules are still needed for crediting methods and quantified removals.
source: Tanzania Forest Services Agency / Ministry of Natural Resources and Tourism
status_note: Final national strategy published on 4 August 2025

subnational_area: Mangroves and associated wetlands in Peru
document_title: Law No. 32099 — Protection, Conservation and Sustainable Use of Wetlands
notes: Peru's Law No. 32099 requires all levels of government and relevant actors to protect, conserve and sustainably use wetlands and to prevent, reduce and mitigate degradation. It expressly covers ecosystems such as mangroves, estuaries, lagoons and deltas and requires consideration of climate mitigation and adaptation. It does not establish blue-carbon accounting or removal targets and therefore primarily protects existing carbon stores and ecosystems.
source: Congress of Peru / Ministry of Environment, SINIA
status_note: In force since publication on 20 July 2024

document_title: REDD+ Ecuador — Natural Heritage Governance, Conservation and Forest Restoration Component
notes: Ecuador's REDD+ policy framework identifies mangroves as vulnerable ecosystems requiring protection and includes active and passive restoration within natural-heritage governance. The component aims to increase carbon reservoirs by maintaining protected area and expanding reforestation and treats ecosystem integrity and connectivity as important conditions for carbon capture and storage.
source: Ministry of Environment of Ecuador / REDD+ Ecuador
status_note: National policy component linked to the 2013–2017 National Development Plan and continuing REDD+ implementation

subnational_area: National mangrove and wetland research sites
document_title: Liberia EPA–IAEA Blue Carbon Laboratory Capacity Programme
notes: Liberia's Environmental Protection Agency received a EUR 100,000 elemental analyzer to measure carbon stocks and accumulation rates in mangroves and wetlands, prepare a national blue-carbon inventory and provide data for climate policy and coastal management. This is MRV and research-capacity building, not a crediting methodology or verified removal.
source: Environmental Protection Agency of Liberia / International Atomic Energy Agency
status_note: Equipment received in September 2025; laboratory and inventory capacity under development

document_title: Executive Order No. 155 — Carbon Markets Authority and National Carbon Registry
notes: Executive Order No. 155 establishes a Carbon Market Authority, national carbon registry and Carbon Investment Fund and authorizes management of carbon projects, including those in the blue economy. The order took immediate effect but prescribes no methodology for mangroves, seagrass, ocean alkalinity enhancement or another marine pathway, so it is recorded as cross-technology market governance.
source: Executive Mansion, Republic of Liberia
status_note: Executive Order issued on 31 October 2025 and effective immediately

document_title: National Wetland Policy — Validation Stage
notes: The Gambia's Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources completed validation of a national wetlands policy intended to create a unified framework for conservation, restoration and wise use and to strengthen governance of wetlands and mangroves. Public information shows validation and policy-coordination activity but does not confirm final adoption or entry into force, so it is recorded as under review.
source: Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Natural Resources, The Gambia
status_note: Policy validated through a national stakeholder workshop in 2026; final adoption not confirmed

document_title: Gabon NDC 3.0 — Angondjé–Ntom Mangrove Restoration and Conservation Project
notes: Gabon NDC 3.0 identifies the Angondjé–Ntom mangrove restoration and conservation project as an unconditional measure for 2023–2043, including demarcation, information signage and nursery construction. It forms part of a broader land-use and forestry package, and the document does not disclose a project-specific CO2-removal estimate.
source: Government of Gabon / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in December 2025; project period 2023–2043

document_title: Madagascar Second NDC — Quantified Mangrove Restoration Carbon Removal
notes: Madagascar's second NDC treats mangrove restoration as a separate land-use and forestry mitigation pathway, estimating a contribution of minus 14,269.3 Gg CO2e by 2030. It also proposes a national mangrove-restoration plan, restoration of 170,000 hectares by 2030 and stronger regional MRV and information systems. The figure is an NDC scenario estimate, not verified project credits.
source: Government of Madagascar / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC submitted in January 2024; target year 2030

subnational_area: Coastal mangrove landscapes including Sherbro and Scarcies
document_title: Sierra Leone NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Rehabilitation and Blue-Carbon Credit Opportunity
notes: Sierra Leone NDC 3.0 identifies mangrove rehabilitation as a coastal-resilience and blue-carbon priority. It presents a potential restoration range of 3,000–30,000 hectares by 2030 and notes possible blue-carbon credits and Paris Agreement Article 6 trading. This is a policy-planning scenario, not issued credits or completed restoration.
source: Government of Sierra Leone / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in December 2025; rehabilitation scale presented as a 2030 opportunity range

document_title: Sierra Leone NDC 3.0 — Blue-Carbon MRV and Credit-Ready Estuary Pilots
notes: NDC 3.0 calls for blue-carbon MRV systems, shoreline-management plans, credit-ready estuary pilots in mangrove and delta ecosystems and accompanying safeguards. This is an accounting and project-preparation measure and does not demonstrate adoption of a uniform methodology or completed project verification.
source: Government of Sierra Leone / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; MRV and credit-ready pilot development committed but project certification not confirmed

document_title: Côte d’Ivoire NDC 3.0 — Restore 2,000 ha of Mangroves for Blue Carbon
notes: Côte d'Ivoire NDC 3.0 measure M21.5 targets restoration of 2,000 hectares of mangroves during 2025–2035 to protect coasts, conserve marine biodiversity and sequester high-potential blue carbon. It is a conditional measure, and the baseline indicates no restored area under this measure in 2025.
source: Government of Côte d’Ivoire / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; conditional implementation target for 2025–2035

document_title: Cabo Verde NDC 3.0 — Blue-Carbon Pre-Feasibility before Carbon-Market Entry
notes: Cabo Verde NDC 3.0 requires national pre-feasibility studies before blue-carbon projects enter Paris Agreement Article 6 or voluntary markets and calls for high integrity, transparency, corresponding adjustments, domestic priority and environmental and social safeguards. It does not prescribe mangroves, seagrass or another specific pathway.
source: Government of Cabo Verde / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; blue-carbon market options gated by a future national pre-feasibility assessment

subnational_area: Priority coastal ecosystems and marine protected areas
document_title: Cabo Verde NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Inventory, Protection and Restoration by 2035
notes: Cabo Verde NDC 3.0 calls for identifying, protecting and restoring priority coastal ecosystems, including seagrass beds, by 2035, incorporating dedicated zones into coastal and marine spatial planning and marine-protected-area management, and using spatial analysis to identify sequestration potential. It provides neither a seagrass-restoration area nor a separate CO2-removal amount.
source: Government of Cabo Verde / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 with 2035 ecosystem-management milestones

document_title: FSM NDC 3.0 — Mangrove and Coastal-Vegetation Protection and Restoration
notes: The Federated States of Micronesia NDC 3.0 identifies protection and restoration of mangroves and coastal vegetation as unconditional measures for natural coastal defense, erosion and storm-surge reduction, and maintenance of nearshore fisheries. It also recognizes mangroves as important carbon stores but provides no separate area or CO2-removal quantity.
source: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted in September 2025; measure classified as unconditional

document_title: FSM NDC 3.0 — Seagrass and Coastal-Wetland Restoration and Carbon Monitoring
notes: NDC 3.0 conditionally targets restoration, management and protection of more than 50% of coastal and marine habitats by 2035 and specifically calls for replanting and community projects to restore degraded seagrass beds and coastal wetlands, together with expanded health monitoring to track sequestration. It provides no separate quantified removal amount.
source: Government of the Federated States of Micronesia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; conditional coastal-habitat target for 2035

document_title: Kiribati Third National Communication — Mangrove Plantation Mitigation Assessment
notes: Kiribati's third national communication assesses mangrove planting as a land-sector mitigation measure, with a scenario increasing annual planting to a cumulative 4.8 hectares restored by 2030 and estimated annual biomass accumulation of 42.5 tCO2 at that point. It notes the lack of specific IPCC guidance for fringe mangroves, so the estimate is a national scenario rather than a binding target or verified credit.
source: Government of Kiribati / UNFCCC
status_note: Third National Communication submitted in May 2026; mitigation estimate based on an assessed 2030 scenario

document_title: Kiribati Third National Communication — Seagrass Protection, Restoration and Monitoring
notes: The third national communication identifies seagrass beds as coastal sinks that absorb and store CO2 and reports that they are protected under environmental legislation; the environment agency is undertaking restoration and monitoring similar to its mangrove work. The document gives no seagrass area, carbon-stock method or quantified removal and is therefore treated as policy reporting and MRV preparation.
source: Government of Kiribati / UNFCCC
status_note: Third National Communication submitted in May 2026; protection and restoration work reported as underway

subnational_area: Chubut Province coastline and associated salt marshes
document_title: Decree No. 1140/2025 — Chubut Climate Response Plan Blue-Carbon Measure
notes: Chubut Province Decree No. 1140/2025 approved a provincial climate response plan that calls for research on carbon-capture potential in the coastal zone and associated salt marshes. It also records an Inter-American Development Bank-supported consultancy to quantify coastal-ecosystem sink capacity, design conservation-finance instruments and prepare the legal and governance framework for a provincial conservation fund. No crediting methodology or quantified removal target has yet been established.
source: Government of Chubut Province — Secretariat of Environment and Sustainable Development Control
status_note: Provincial climate plan approved by Decree No. 1140/2025 on 16 September 2025

document_title: Vanuatu NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Forests, Wetlands and Shoreline Trees Conservation
notes: Vanuatu NDC 3.0 commits to protecting, conserving and sustainably managing mangroves, mangrove ecosystems, wetlands and coastal vegetation to improve climate resilience. It proposes grants or concessional finance for community nurseries, monitoring plots, buffer-zone restoration and mangrove conservation but gives no separate area or CO2-removal amount.
source: Government of Vanuatu / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 24 September 2025

document_title: Vanuatu NDC 3.0 — MACBLUE Mangrove Distribution Mapping
notes: NDC 3.0 lists the MACBLUE project for mapping the distribution of mangroves and seagrass beds. This record covers only the mangrove spatial baseline and monitoring preparation; the document does not show that mapping has become a national greenhouse-gas inventory method or generated verified removals.
source: Government of Vanuatu / UNFCCC / MACBLUE
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; mapping activity identified as an implementation and evidence-building measure

document_title: Vanuatu NDC 3.0 — MACBLUE Seagrass Distribution Mapping
notes: The same NDC lists MACBLUE mapping of seagrass distribution as a blue-carbon evidence-building activity. This record is separated from mangrove mapping to enable ecosystem-specific screening. Public documents provide no seagrass area, carbon-stock method or quantified removal target.
source: Government of Vanuatu / UNFCCC / MACBLUE
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; mapping activity identified as an implementation and evidence-building measure

document_title: Honduras NDC 3.0 — Restore at Least 10% of Mangrove Forests by 2035
notes: Honduras NDC 3.0 targets restoration of at least 10% of national mangroves by 2035 within sustainable and climate-resilient management of marine and coastal ecosystems. It quantifies an ecosystem-restoration proportion but provides no separate tCO2-removal amount or credit-issuance scale.
source: Government of Honduras / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 21 January 2026; target year 2035

document_title: Honduras NDC 3.0 — National Seagrass Coverage Baseline by 2035
notes: Honduras NDC 3.0 requires establishment of a national seagrass-cover baseline by 2035 to identify vulnerable and high-risk areas. This is spatial-baseline, monitoring and policy preparation rather than a restoration-area target, carbon-stock methodology or achieved removal.
source: Government of Honduras / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 21 January 2026; baseline milestone for 2035

document_title: Timor-Leste NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Restoration, Expansion and Investment Plan
notes: Timor-Leste NDC 3.0 identifies mangrove restoration and expansion as nature-positive measures that enhance coastal protection, natural carbon sequestration and biodiversity and calls for stronger mangrove protection and enhancement. The forestry authority, FAO and a national technical working group are preparing a Mangrove Restoration and Investment Plan. The commitment is conditional on climate finance and technical assistance and sets no separate area or removal quantity.
source: Government of Timor-Leste / UNFCCC / FAO
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 9 June 2026; conditional Mangrove Restoration and Investment Plan under development

subnational_area: Atauro Island and other coastal areas
document_title: National Blue Economy Policy and Action Plan 2025–2035 — Seagrass Conservation and Restoration
notes: Timor-Leste's blue-economy policy framework supports bottom-up conservation and restoration of marine and coastal ecosystems, expressly focusing on seagrass and mangroves in places such as Atauro Island. The NDC also recognizes the role of seagrass in capturing atmospheric carbon. It sets no separate seagrass-restoration area, carbon-accounting method or removal quantity.
source: Government of Timor-Leste — Council of Ministers / UNFCCC
status_note: Blue Economy Policy and Action Plan formally approved by the Council of Ministers on 20 February 2026

document_title: National Blue Economy Policy and Action Plan 2025–2035 — Marine Algae and Seaweed Carbon Sequestration
notes: NDC 3.0 states that seaweed production can contribute to natural greenhouse-gas removal, and the blue-economy action plan includes development of the sequestration potential of marine algae and seaweed. It does not specify a durable post-harvest storage pathway, permanence, leakage or MRV method, so the record captures policy direction without treating all seaweed production as permanent negative emissions.
source: Government of Timor-Leste — Council of Ministers / UNFCCC
status_note: Approved national Blue Economy Policy and Action Plan; implementation period 2025–2035

document_title: Timor-Leste NDC 3.0 — Blue-Carbon and Marine-Zone Carbon-Market Framework
notes: NDC 3.0 proposes a policy framework enabling local communities to aggregate activities and participate in international carbon-trading platforms, including protection of marine areas, blue-carbon reservoirs and other ecological restoration. It also calls for use of Paris Agreement Article 6 and emerging global carbon-market opportunities. Methodologies, corresponding adjustments, registries and verification systems remain to be developed, so it is classified as market preparation.
source: Government of Timor-Leste / UNFCCC
status_note: Conditional NDC commitment; policy, registry and methodology details remain under development

subnational_area: Bobonaro Municipality and selected national mangrove sites
document_title: RESTORE / FAO Mangrove Conservation and Restoration — Mapping, Community Capacity and Investment Preparation
notes: A 2025 mangrove survey and ecological assessment in Bobonaro, Timor-Leste, identified restoration sites and community-management options. The FAO mangrove project runs from January 2025 to July 2026 and aims to improve knowledge and capacity, strengthen community participation, create restoration investment and support scale-up. It supports blue-carbon sequestration but has not generated verified project removals.
source: FAO / Government of Timor-Leste / Kiwa Initiative RESTORE partners
status_note: Ongoing official programme, 1 January 2025–31 July 2026

subnational_area: Priority coastal zones across Grande Comore, Anjouan and Mohéli
document_title: Comoros NDC 3.0 — Restore 1,000 ha of Mangroves by 2035
notes: Comoros NDC 3.0 expressly calls for mangrove replanting within 2025–2035 coastal and marine actions and uses restored mangrove area as a scientific-monitoring indicator, with an expected result of 1,000 hectares restored. It recognizes both coastal-protection and blue-carbon benefits but provides no separate tCO2-removal estimate.
source: Government of the Union of the Comoros / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 30 March 2026; implementation period 2025–2035

document_title: Comoros NDC 3.0 — Seagrass Meadow Rehabilitation
notes: The same NDC identifies restoration of degraded seagrass beds as a specific marine-ecosystem action and uses restored mangrove and seagrass area as a monitoring indicator. It assigns no separate area or carbon-removal quantity to seagrass, so the record captures a formal restoration direction rather than quantified negative emissions.
source: Government of the Union of the Comoros / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 30 March 2026; seagrass rehabilitation included in the 2025–2035 action framework
