document_title: Comoros NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Blue-Carbon MRV and Carbon-Credit Governance
notes: Comoros NDC 3.0 states that mangrove restoration could generate blue-carbon credits based on removals but that credible credits require MRV, baselines and institutional architecture that are not yet in place. Near-term priorities include stronger inventories and MRV, credit governance and benefit sharing, environmental and social safeguards, and exploration of Paris Agreement Article 6-compatible coastal and mangrove credits. This is market and accounting preparation, not an adopted methodology.
source: Government of the Union of the Comoros / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; carbon-credit architecture and MRV capacity remain under development

document_title: Eritrea NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Afforestation, Policy Expansion and Carbon-Sink Enhancement
notes: Eritrea NDC 3.0 calls for strengthening mangrove-restoration and expansion targets and policies because mangroves store more carbon per unit area than terrestrial forests and reports approximately 456.5 hectares planted since 2018. Its estimate of 93.13 ktCO2 per year covers both 7,880 hectares of terrestrial afforestation and 456.5 hectares of mangroves and cannot be attributed solely to mangroves, so it is not recorded as a stand-alone mangrove-removal amount.
source: Government of the State of Eritrea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 18 February 2026; 456.5 ha of mangrove plantation reported as implemented since 2018

document_title: Eritrea NDC 3.0 — Zula–Foro Community Mangrove Rehabilitation Project
notes: Eritrea NDC 3.0's marine-resource investment portfolio includes a community-based mangrove ecosystem restoration and rehabilitation project in the Zula and Foro sub-zones, with a total budget of USD 100,000 split equally between domestic funding and international support needs and performance measured in hectares restored. It provides no fixed area or project-level carbon accounting and is therefore recorded as a formal implementation investment rather than verified removal.
source: Government of the State of Eritrea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; project included in the national adaptation investment portfolio with mixed domestic and international financing

document_title: Guinea NDC 3.0 — Restore at Least 5,000 ha of Mangroves
notes: Guinea NDC 3.0 calls for restoration of at least 5,000 hectares of mangroves within forest, biodiversity and protected-area investment needs and separately identifies mangrove restoration and nature-based solutions in coastal measures. The target combines adaptation, biodiversity and blue-carbon mitigation benefits but provides no separate tCO2-removal estimate.
source: Government of the Republic of Guinea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0 submitted on 6 November 2025

document_title: Guinea NDC 3.0 — Mangrove Blue-Carbon Credits, Article 6 and Coastal Adaptation Fund
notes: NDC 3.0 proposes financing coastal restoration through blue-carbon projects such as mangrove credits and establishing a local coastal-adaptation fund by 2028, supported by port and industrial revenues. It also calls for voluntary-market and Paris Agreement Article 6 finance and certification of mangrove-restoration credits under international standards. Because national methodologies, registry arrangements, corresponding adjustments and project verification are not confirmed, this is market preparation rather than an adopted crediting method.
source: Government of the Republic of Guinea / UNFCCC
status_note: Active NDC 3.0; blue-carbon project certification and Article 6 arrangements remain under development

document_title: Guinea-Bissau Updated NDC — Mangrove and Wetland Restoration Integrated with Mitigation and REDD+
notes: Guinea-Bissau's updated NDC identifies wetlands and mangroves as priorities for deployment and strengthening in forestry, biodiversity and protected-area policy and calls for linking them with mitigation, ecosystem restoration and REDD+ programmes. They remain priority areas requiring new projects and finance, with no mangrove-area or stand-alone removal target.
source: Government of Guinea-Bissau / UNFCCC
status_note: Active updated NDC submitted in 2021; implementation depends on new programmes and finance

document_title: Indonesia Second NDC — Mangrove GHG Inventory, FREL and REDD+ Accounting
notes: Indonesia's second NDC confirms that mangroves are included in the national greenhouse-gas inventory as wetlands and in the REDD+ forest reference emission level and results estimates and states that the marine-accounting framework is integrating marine and coastal ecosystem data. This records an operating formal accounting inclusion but does not mean every mangrove-restoration project automatically qualifies for credits.
source: Government of the Republic of Indonesia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC submitted on 27 October 2025; mangrove inventory and FREL/REDD+ accounting reported as established

document_title: Indonesia Second NDC — Seagrass National Map, GHG Methodology and Future NDC Integration
notes: Indonesia's second NDC states that the government is updating the national seagrass map, developing methods for estimating seagrass greenhouse gases and identifying mitigation actions for possible inclusion in future NDCs. Spatial-planning and coastal-restoration regulations already exist, but seagrass remains at the mapping, methodological and policy-integration stage and cannot yet be treated as a formal national removal amount or crediting method.
source: Government of the Republic of Indonesia / UNFCCC
status_note: Active Second NDC submitted on 27 October 2025; mapping and methodology development ongoing

document_title: Global Ocean Negative Carbon Emission (Global ONCE) — UN Ocean Decade Programme
notes: The Global ONCE programme, endorsed under the UN Decade of Ocean Science, is building an international network of observation and experimental facilities, coordinating ocean negative-emissions research and developing an assessment framework for mitigation and adaptation options. It covers approaches including land–sea coordinated sink enhancement and artificial upwelling. The programme is a research and evaluation platform, not deployment authorization for a specific project, and it makes no quantified removal commitment.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade
status_note: Active UN Ocean Decade Programme, 2022–2030

document_title: Global Ocean Decade Programme for Blue Carbon (GO-BC)
notes: The UN Ocean Decade's Global Ocean Blue Carbon programme coordinates cross-regional blue-carbon research, capacity building and knowledge translation for policymakers and expands research from traditional coastal blue-carbon ecosystems across the estuary–coast–open-ocean continuum. It primarily builds research and collaboration networks and is not itself a restoration project or carbon-crediting mechanism.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade
status_note: Active UN Ocean Decade Programme, 2022–2030

document_title: OceanNETs — Ocean-based Negative Emission Technologies
notes: OceanNETs was a Horizon 2020 research and innovation project assessing the effectiveness, sustainability, ecological risks, costs, public acceptance and governance of ocean negative-emissions technologies and conducting experiments and scenario studies on pathways such as OAE and macroalgae. It ended in 2025 and produced research and policy recommendations but not deployment authorization or a uniform regulatory standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon 2020 project completed on 30 June 2025

document_title: SEAO2-CDR — Strategies for the Evaluation and Assessment of Ocean-based Carbon Dioxide Removal
notes: SEAO2-CDR is a Horizon Europe project developing evaluation pathways and methods for marine carbon dioxide removal, including verification, monitoring, economics, environmental impacts, ethics and governance, in cooperation with industry and regulators. It remains in the research and method-development phase and has not created binding MRV rules, a crediting methodology or deployment permits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Active Horizon Europe project, 1 June 2023–31 May 2027

subnational_area: German North Sea and other marine research areas
document_title: CDRmare — Marine Carbon Sinks in Decarbonisation Pathways
notes: CDRmare is a German Marine Research Alliance mission funded by federal ministries and northern coastal states to study marine carbon removal and storage, including OAE, vegetated coastal sinks, artificial upwelling and subseabed geological storage, and to develop interdisciplinary assessment, monitoring, attribution and accounting approaches. It is in its second funding period and remains research and experimentation rather than commercial deployment authorization.
source: German Marine Research Alliance (DAM) / Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space
status_note: Active research mission; second funding phase runs through July 2027

document_title: Global MSP 2060 under the ONCE Programme
notes: This UN Ocean Decade project under Global ONCE studies the scale, distribution, stocks, fluxes and drivers of ocean carbon sinks and develops theory, methods and marine-spatial-planning approaches for natural and artificially enhanced sink zones. It provides a scientific basis for future planning but has not designated legally binding carbon-sink zones or authorized deployment.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / First Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, China
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2025–2030

document_title: Sediment Upheaval and Negative Carbon Emissions
notes: This Global ONCE Ocean Decade project combines multidimensional observations and numerical modelling to analyze estuarine sediment–water processes, suspended-sediment dispersal and their effects on carbon emissions and sink potential, providing evidence for possible estuarine sink-enhancement options. It remains mechanism research and option assessment, not direct implementation, and reports no verified removals.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / China University of Petroleum
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2025–2030

document_title: Carbon Cycles in Huang–Bohai Sea Wetlands
notes: This Global ONCE Ocean Decade project compares carbon cycles and controls across different delta wetlands of the Yellow and Bohai seas and develops a multidimensional coastal-wetland carbon-budget model to support blue-carbon enhancement practice. It primarily produces models and knowledge and has not implemented large-scale restoration or created an official accounting methodology.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Qingdao Institute of Marine Geology
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2025–2030

subnational_area: Pearl River Estuary and Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area
document_title: Intelligent Coastal-Urban-Bay CO2 Emission Studies (iCUBES)
notes: This Global ONCE Ocean Decade project is building an intelligent three-dimensional marine ecological monitoring system across spatial, temporal and governance dimensions in the Pearl River Estuary–Greater Bay Area and using international bay cooperation to support carbon-neutral and negative-emissions governance in coastal city–bay complexes. It currently builds monitoring and evidence systems and does not authorize a specific negative-emissions project.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Southern University of Science and Technology
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2024–2030

document_title: Sea the Value — Blue Carbon Valuation and Finance Project
notes: This interdisciplinary Global ONCE project assessed the multiple values of blue carbon, biodiversity and marine water quality and co-developed green-investment options and financial mechanisms supporting conservation and restoration of blue-carbon ecosystems. It concluded in 2025 and produced valuation and policy-relevant knowledge but did not establish a formal credit-issuance system or mandatory financial regime.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Plymouth Marine Laboratory
status_note: Ocean Decade project completed on 31 August 2025

subnational_area: North Pacific and Southern Ocean research areas
document_title: Exploring the Potential of Ocean Blue Carbon
notes: This Global Ocean Blue Carbon project studies atmosphere–land–ocean carbon exchange, marine uptake and storage, feedbacks involving warming, acidification and deoxygenation, and blue-carbon ecosystem services, and develops foundational technologies for understanding and managing the ocean–CO2 relationship. It remains research and technology development, not engineering deployment or verified removals.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Atmosphere and Ocean Research Institute, University of Tokyo
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, October 2023–March 2031

document_title: Demonstrating Ocean CDR with Hydrogen Production
notes: This UN Ocean Decade demonstration project plans a larger modular seawater-electrolysis facility in Singapore to test CO2 removal from seawater together with low-carbon hydrogen production, environmental safety and monitoring systems. It is an active technology demonstration, but public materials do not show general deployment authorization, an approved crediting methodology or verified large-scale removals.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Equatic
status_note: Active Ocean Decade demonstration project, 2026–2028

subnational_area: Canadian Arctic, Atlantic and Pacific coasts
document_title: Blue Carbon Canada
notes: This Canadian Global Ocean Blue Carbon project quantifies current and potential future carbon storage in salt marshes, seagrass beds, kelp forests and seabed sediments, assesses bottom-trawling impacts and ecological and economic value, and identifies priority protection and restoration areas to support climate-smart management. It remains research and policy preparation and does not mean Canada has formally included all relevant stores in national inventory or carbon-market accounting.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / University of Victoria
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, July 2022–August 2028

document_title: European Regional Hub for Blue Carbon (Euro-BC)
notes: The European regional hub of Global Ocean Blue Carbon is building an interdisciplinary network, databases on habitat extent and vulnerability, repositories of carbon stocks and sequestration rates, and a blue-carbon policy roadmap linked to European legislative drivers. It remains a knowledge-sharing, database and roadmap initiative and has not created a uniform EU accounting standard or binding blue-carbon rules.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / JPI Oceans
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, May 2023–April 2027

document_title: Chinese Regional Hub for Blue Carbon (China-BC)
notes: The China regional hub of Global Ocean Blue Carbon connects science, policy and public communication, facilitates knowledge exchange between Chinese and international blue-carbon programmes and uses research to support national policymaking and ecosystem-protection practice. It is a research coordination and policy-translation platform, not a source of mandatory standards, crediting mechanisms or specific restoration targets.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Third Institute of Oceanography, Ministry of Natural Resources, China
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2024–2029

document_title: Convex Seascape Survey
notes: This Global Ocean Blue Carbon research collaboration investigates the sources, mechanisms and spatial distribution of carbon burial on continental shelves and the effects of human disturbance and protection, providing evidence for ocean-use decisions and nature-based climate solutions. It addresses knowledge gaps but does not itself establish protection rules, restoration projects or tradable credits.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Blue Marine Foundation
status_note: Active Ocean Decade project, 2022–2027

document_title: CDRmare HUB Workshop Report — Monitoring Environmental Impacts of mCDR Field Tests
notes: CDRmare's report on environmental monitoring for marine CDR field trials summarizes expert discussions from six countries on minimum monitoring needs, knowledge gaps, stakeholder participation and environmental review and notes inconsistencies among regional, national and international rules. It informs research and regulatory design but is non-binding and does not establish a uniform international environmental MRV standard.
source: CDRmare / German Marine Research Alliance
status_note: Published in March 2026 as a non-binding workshop report

subnational_area: Global network of ocean-climate innovation hubs
document_title: Global Ecosystem for Ocean Solutions (GEOS)
notes: The UN Ocean Decade-endorsed Global Ecosystem for Ocean Solutions programme builds a cross-sector and cross-regional ocean–climate innovation network connecting scientists, businesses, public bodies and communities to develop and test solutions, including marine CDR, blue-carbon restoration and ocean-carbon observation. It provides coordination, knowledge exchange and decision support and is not itself a permit or credit certification.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Ocean Visions
status_note: Ocean Decade programme active from 18 May 2021 to 31 December 2030

subnational_area: Southeast Asia and the Indo-West Pacific
document_title: International Blue Carbon Institute
notes: The International Blue Carbon Institute, a Global Ocean Blue Carbon project, works with governments, researchers and communities to translate science into policy, finance, tools, best practice and implementation strategies, particularly for mangroves and seagrass in Southeast Asia and the Indo-Pacific. It provides policy and methodological support but public information does not show that it issues credits or creates a legally binding uniform standard.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Conservation International
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 September 2023 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Blue Carbon for Sustainable Development
notes: This Global Ocean Blue Carbon project supports Kenya in integrating blue carbon into national development and climate agendas and reducing degradation through conservation, restoration and sustainable use of mangroves, seagrass and tidal wetlands, while strengthening government coordination, stakeholder capacity and community benefits. Public targets provide no additional-removal quantity and do not establish a credit-issuance mechanism.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Kenya Marine and Fisheries Research Institute
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 23 December 2022 to 31 December 2027

document_title: The Observatory of Mangrove and its Maretories
notes: This Global Ocean Blue Carbon project focuses on mangroves in the Brazilian Amazon and Peru and builds monitoring based on citizen science, participatory GIS and local knowledge to support governance, public-policy coordination and community participation. Its emphasis is observation and governance capacity rather than quantified additional removals or authorization of specific restoration works.
source: UN Ocean Decade / OSC Sarambuí
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 15 November 2022 to 20 December 2027

subnational_area: France and French Guiana, Spain and Canada pilot areas
document_title: Coastal Blue Carbon from Space
notes: This Ocean Decade action, linked to a European Space Agency project, uses open Earth-observation data including Copernicus to develop methods for mapping and assessing carbon stocks in mangroves, seagrass and salt marshes and to provide decision tools for governments and coastal managers. It creates prototype observation and accounting capacity, not an effective carbon-accounting standard or restoration authorization.
source: UN Ocean Decade / European Space Agency programme / i-Sea
status_note: Project ran from 1 March 2024 to 1 March 2026 and has ended

document_title: North Atlantic Carbon Observatory
notes: This Ocean Decade project plans a multinational North Atlantic carbon-observation platform connecting government bodies, research networks, industry and data providers to deliver sustained, integrated, climate-scale marine carbon measurements and support accountable marine-CDR monitoring. It is observation infrastructure and MRV evidence building, not deployment authorization for a specific technology.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Ocean Frontier Institute
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 31 August 2024 to 6 August 2030

subnational_area: Projects across the Indian, North Atlantic and North Pacific oceans
document_title: Blue Ocean Credits Program
notes: The Blue Ocean Credits programme combines research on mangroves, seagrass, seaweed and low-trophic aquaculture with ecological restoration, remote sensing, capacity building and development of blue-carbon and biodiversity credit systems. Credit-system development is a formal workstream, but public information does not demonstrate completion of a uniform methodology, registry or actual credit issuance.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Reef Aquaculture Conservancy
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 November 2022 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Protect Restore Ocean Capital and Blue Economies (PROCARIBE+)
notes: The GEF-cofinanced PROCARIBE+ programme advances protection and restoration of coastal and marine natural capital, blue-carbon action, community small grants, marine spatial planning, regional governance and investment in a climate-resilient blue economy across the Wider Caribbean. Blue carbon is an explicit workstream, but public targets do not separately report achieved removals or issued credits.
source: UN Ocean Decade / UNOPS / UNDP / Global Environment Facility
status_note: Regional programme active from 5 May 2023 to 4 May 2028

document_title: Governing Changing Oceans
notes: This Ocean Decade project studies governance transitions for emerging marine climate interventions such as seaweed cultivation and marine CDR and works with practitioners in blue carbon, finance, conservation, Indigenous governance and community resilience to advise governments, industry and donors on governance and risk. It builds research and policy knowledge, creates no permitting duties and does not endorse commercial deployment.
source: UN Ocean Decade / University of Melbourne
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Tēnaka Mangrove Project
notes: This Ocean Decade project restores mangroves in Malaysian Borneo and plans to expand restoration sites, collecting quarterly ecological and biodiversity data and developing eDNA and blue-carbon calculation tools for impact reporting. Public materials describe restoration and monitoring but do not show verified or issued credits.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Tēnaka
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2031

subnational_area: Community-led restoration sites across multiple ocean basins
document_title: SeaTrees: Community-Powered Ocean Restoration
notes: The SeaTrees Ocean Decade action organizes community-led protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrass, kelp, coral reefs and coastal watersheds, combining carbon-sink, biodiversity and local sustainable-development objectives. Public information provides no uniform accounting of additional removals and does not indicate that SeaTrees itself is a crediting standard.
source: UN Ocean Decade / SeaTrees
status_note: Ocean Decade action active from 4 March 2018 to 31 December 2030

subnational_area: Brunei and Borneo coasts, South China Sea
document_title: Borneo Ocean Resilience 4Nature, Economy, Outreach
notes: This Ocean Decade action plans artificial reefs, community mangrove planting, an oyster hatchery and a kelp pilot during 2025–2030 and proposes AI, IoT, eDNA and remote-sensing monitoring of blue carbon and ecological recovery, with future carbon credits as an objective. The credits remain a project goal and public information does not demonstrate validated methodology or issuance.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Poni Group
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 May 2023 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Aotearoa New Zealand Marine Carbon Forum
notes: This Ocean Decade project provides independent assessment of New Zealand's natural marine carbon sinks and brings together researchers, government, policymakers, private actors and Iwi/Māori to support a national strategy comparing benefits and risks of marine capture and storage approaches. It remains research and coordination and does not authorize deployment.
source: UN Ocean Decade / University of Otago
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 2 January 2025 to 31 January 2028

document_title: Caspian Sea Carbon Dioxide Removal Project (CaspianCDR)
notes: CaspianCDR is an Ocean Decade-endorsed research project studying microalgae cultivation using Caspian Sea water and photosynthesis to remove CO2, drawing on concepts for large open ponds in coastal deserts. It remains technology research and has not demonstrated scaled deployment, verified durable storage or credit issuance.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Caspian Environmental Consortium Ltd.
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 2 May 2023 to 31 December 2027

subnational_area: Eastern Canadian seagrass beds and kelp forests
document_title: Blue Carbon Assessment for Seagrass and Kelp
notes: This Fisheries and Oceans Canada-led Ocean Decade project established the first regional carbon budget for eelgrass beds and kelp forests in eastern Canada, addressing uncertainties in carbon export, deep-sea deposition and global blue-carbon estimates to inform valuation and management. The completed project is research and accounting, not restoration or credit certification.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Fisheries and Oceans Canada
status_note: Project ran from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2025 and is completed

document_title: Nazaré Artificial Reefs Seaweed Planting Pilot
notes: This Ocean Decade pilot cultivates seaweed on an artificial reef south of Nazaré Harbour, Portugal, to restore ecosystems, increase biodiversity and provide alternative livelihoods for fishing communities. Project materials mention climate benefits but provide no verified net-removal quantity, durable storage pathway or carbon-credit outcome.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Hope Zones Foundation
status_note: Pilot ran from 8 March 2023 to 6 September 2025 and has ended

subnational_area: Giant kelp cultivation and restoration sites
document_title: Rewilding the Oceans with Giant Kelp (Kelp Blue)
notes: This Ocean Decade project scales cultivation of giant-kelp forests to restore marine ecosystems, increase biodiversity and harvest canopy biomass for low-carbon products. It treats kelp CO2 uptake as a climate benefit, but public information does not disclose independently verified net removal, additionality or long-term storage fraction.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Kelp Blue
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 31 August 2023 to 31 August 2027

subnational_area: Kelp restoration operations including Japan, North America and Norway
document_title: Urchinomics: Global Kelp Forest Restoration Sea Urchin Ranching Alliance
notes: The Urchinomics Ocean Decade project removes overgrazing sea urchins, fattens and sells them in aquaculture systems and restores kelp forests through a self-sustaining restoration business model. It has connections with Japanese blue-carbon credit practice, but this record concerns the global restoration project and does not treat it as a generally applicable crediting standard.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Urchinomics
status_note: Ocean Decade action started on 1 January 2021; no formal end date is stated

subnational_area: European coastal seas, Dutch Antilles, Black Sea and southern China coast
document_title: C-BLUES — Carbon Sequestration in Blue Ecosystems
notes: The EU C-BLUES project studies carbon stocks and greenhouse-gas fluxes in seagrass, tidal wetlands, mangroves, macroalgae and macroalgal aquaculture, develops spatial maps, standard operating procedures and accounting best practice, and contributes evidence for future IPCC Wetlands Supplement updates and national inventories under the UNFCCC. It develops methods but is not itself an adopted international standard.
source: European Commission CORDIS / Horizon Europe
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2028

subnational_area: Pilot sites in Germany, Jersey and the Maldives
document_title: COASTS — Coastal Observation Advances Leveraging Space Technology Services
notes: The EU COASTS project integrates Earth observation, advanced modelling and coastal-geomorphology models to develop a blue-carbon coastal-observation service focused on mangroves, seagrass and salt marshes, with pilots in Germany, Jersey and Maldives. It produces monitoring and decision services rather than implementing restoration or establishing an effective MRV standard.
source: European Commission CORDIS / Horizon Europe
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 November 2024 to 31 October 2027

document_title: TRAMAE — Response of Coccolithophores to Trace Metals and Alkalinity Enhancement
notes: The EU TRAMAE project assesses how trace metals associated with ocean alkalinity enhancement and alkaline-mineral release affect coccolithophores, calcification and plankton ecosystems and whether these responses enhance or offset OAE efficiency. It is ecological-risk and mechanism research, not authorization for ocean deployment.
source: European Commission CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: EU-funded research project active from 1 February 2024 to 31 August 2027

document_title: SCaLED — Seagrass Carbon Cycling and Local Environmental Drivers
notes: The EU SCaLED project combined ecological, biogeochemical, eddy-covariance and spatial modelling to estimate carbon cycling and sequestration in seagrass and predict climate responses for coastal management and regional policy. CORDIS states that the project was terminated early on 31 May 2024, so it is not classified as active.
source: European Commission CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Project started 1 March 2023 and was terminated on 31 May 2024

subnational_area: Marine diatom blooms, sinking particles and sediments
document_title: C-Quest — Discover Molecular Pathways for Marine Glyco-Carbon Sequestration
notes: The ERC-funded C-Quest project examines whether polysaccharides produced by marine diatoms resist bacterial degradation and contribute to long-term storage, tracking sugar carbon through blooms, sinking particles and sediments. It investigates mechanisms related to the microbial and biological carbon pumps and is not an engineered deployment or policy authorization.
source: European Commission CORDIS / European Research Council
status_note: ERC project active from 1 October 2022 to 30 September 2027

document_title: RESCUE — Response of the Earth System to Overshoot, Climate Neutrality and Negative Emissions
notes: The EU RESCUE project incorporates ocean alkalinity enhancement and macroalgae cultivation into Earth-system and integrated-assessment models and overshoot scenarios to assess climate, ecological and economic effects. Marine CDR is one part of a broader negative-emissions research portfolio, and the project provides scenario evidence rather than implementing ocean engineering.
source: European Commission CORDIS / Horizon Europe
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2026

subnational_area: Eleven funded projects across eight U.S. states
document_title: Sensing Exports of Anthropogenic Carbon Through Ocean Observation (SEA-CO2) Program
notes: The U.S. Department of Energy's ARPA-E SEA-CO2 programme funds scalable marine-CDR sensors, regional ocean-carbon transport models and data-driven accounting frameworks to reduce MRV uncertainty and support high-quality credits. It validates tools and does not constitute federal endorsement of scaled deployment of a specific technology.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: Program launched in 2023; multiple funded projects remain active through 2027

document_title: NOAA–DOE Memorandum of Agreement on Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal Research and Development
notes: NOAA and the U.S. Department of Energy signed the first formal federal memorandum on marine CDR, covering coordinated research, infrastructure and data collaboration, development of accountable science-based protocols, ecological safety, social benefits and economic feasibility. It strengthens interagency cooperation but does not approve project deployment.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / NOAA
status_note: Formal interagency memorandum signed on 6 June 2024 with no stated expiry

document_title: Sequim Bay Electrochemical Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Field Trial
notes: NOAA, PNNL, the University of Washington and Ebb Carbon completed two small electrochemical OAE discharge trials in November 2024 and February 2025, increasing treated water from about 7,000 to 47,000 gallons and monitoring within existing permit limits. The trials found highly localized chemical signals and tested safety and monitoring feasibility; they do not establish verified large-scale net removal.
source: NOAA Ocean Acidification Program / PNNL / Ebb Carbon
status_note: Two controlled field experiments were completed in November 2024 and February 2025

subnational_area: Marine CDR sites and regional ocean models
document_title: atdepth MRV — Scalable Real-Time GPU Modelling for Marine CDR
notes: ARPA-E funded atdepth MRV to build a GPU-based ocean-simulation system linking global processes with metre-scale turbulence for near-real-time quantification of marine-CDR removals, environmental effects and co-benefits. The objective is an MRV tool, not formal certification as an accounting methodology.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: ARPA-E project active from 14 May 2024 to 13 May 2027

subnational_area: Ocean fertilization modelling and deep-ocean carbon export
document_title: Bigelow Zooplankton-Mediated Carbon Export MRV Project
notes: ARPA-E funded Bigelow Laboratory to develop zooplankton-mediated carbon-export models and an accounting protocol specifically for ocean fertilization to reduce uncertainty in biological-pump and deep-ocean export estimates. It supports MRV development and does not mean the United States has authorized ocean fertilization.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: ARPA-E project active from 18 March 2024 to 17 March 2027

document_title: Caltech Offshore Stand-Alone System for Efficient CO2 Removal from Ocean Water
notes: ARPA-E funded Caltech to develop an offshore stand-alone seawater CO2-capture system using high-current-density electrodialysis stacks and membrane contactors to reduce water throughput and cost. Targets below USD 100 per tonne and multi-gigaton potential are research goals, not verified commercial costs or scaled results.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: ARPA-E project ran from 17 June 2021 to 30 September 2023

document_title: AMENDER — Seawater-Mediated Electrochemical Carbon Dioxide Removal
notes: ARPA-E funded UCLA's AMENDER electrochemical seawater-CDR process, which uses alkaline seawater cations to store CO2 as dissolved or solid carbonates, enables treated water to reabsorb atmospheric CO2 and co-produces hydrogen. The completed project set cost and gigaton-scale goals but did not produce deployment authorization or a credit methodology.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: ARPA-E project ran from 24 June 2022 to 23 December 2025

subnational_area: Autonomous ocean sensing for particulate carbon export
document_title: WHOI Autonomous Thorium Sensor for Marine CDR Carbon-Flux Quantification
notes: ARPA-E funded Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution to develop autonomous sensors using natural thorium-234 decay to quantify sinking particulate organic carbon from gliders, floats and autonomous platforms for MRV of ocean fertilization, artificial upwelling, seaweed cultivation and OAE. ARPA-E lists the project as alumni, so it is classified as ended.
source: U.S. Department of Energy / ARPA-E
status_note: ARPA-E page marks the project as Alumni; listed award period is 1 May 2024 to 30 April 2027

subnational_area: West African coastline and Gulf of Guinea
document_title: Marine Innovation Hub — Ghana
notes: This 2026 Ocean Decade action establishes a marine-climate innovation hub in Ghana, connecting academia, government, communities and NGOs to identify, design and implement ocean-climate projects, including marine CDR, and to promote public knowledge and scalable interventions. It is currently a coordination and capacity-building platform without a specified marine-CDR pathway or deployment authorization.
source: UN Ocean Decade / Emerging Climate Frontiers
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 June 2026 to 30 June 2030

document_title: OSPAR Decision 2007/1 to Prohibit the Storage of Carbon Dioxide Streams in the Water Column or on the Sea-bed
notes: The decision prohibits direct placement of CO2 streams into the water column or on the seabed and entered into effect on 15 January 2008. It addresses marine-disposal practices that may harm ecosystems, does not prohibit appropriately regulated subseabed geological storage and is not a permit for a specific project.
source: OSPAR Commission
status_note: Adopted in 2007; entered into force on 15 January 2008

document_title: OSPAR Decision 2007/2 on the Storage of Carbon Dioxide Streams in Geological Formations
notes: The decision requires Parties to subject subseabed geological storage to authorization or regulation and to issue permits only after comprehensive risk assessment. Permits must address injection volume, CO2-stream composition, transport, monitoring and reporting, remediation and post-closure management, with the objective of permanent storage and prevention of significant adverse effects on the marine environment, health and legitimate uses.
source: OSPAR Commission
status_note: Adopted in 2007; applicable to permits and approvals for geological storage

document_title: OSPAR Agreement 2007-12 — Guidelines for Risk Assessment and Management of Storage of CO2 Streams in Geological Formations
notes: The guidelines establish procedures for site screening, risk characterization, exposure and effects assessment, monitoring, mitigation, closure and long-term management of subseabed CO2 storage to support implementation of OSPAR Decision 2007/2. They provide a review framework but do not replace national permits or authorize specific injection projects.
source: OSPAR Commission
status_note: Adopted guidance supporting implementation of OSPAR Decision 2007/2

document_title: Resolution LP.1(1) — Amendment to Include CO2 Sequestration in Sub-seabed Geological Formations in Annex 1 to the London Protocol
notes: The amendment added eligible CO2 streams to the London Protocol list of materials that may be considered for subseabed geological storage, enabling Parties to authorize permanent storage subject to permitting, waste-stream composition controls and environmental assessment. It entered into force in 2007 but does not automatically authorize a specific site.
source: International Maritime Organization — London Protocol
status_note: Adopted in 2006 and entered into force in 2007

document_title: Resolution LP.3(4) — Amendment to Article 6 of the London Protocol on Export of CO2 Streams for Sub-seabed Storage
notes: The amendment to London Protocol Article 6 allows Parties to export CO2 across borders for subseabed geological storage when bilateral or multilateral arrangements allocate permitting and responsibility and meet Protocol safeguards. As of 2026, it had not received enough acceptances to enter formally into force.
source: International Maritime Organization — London Protocol
status_note: Adopted in 2009; not yet in force pending sufficient acceptances

document_title: Resolution LP.5(14) on the Provisional Application of the 2009 Amendment to Article 6 of the London Protocol
notes: The resolution allows Parties that submit a formal declaration to provisionally apply the 2009 cross-border export amendment before its formal entry into force and requires notification to IMO of interstate arrangements, permits and allocation of responsibilities. It provides a transitional legal route only for countries completing the declaration and notification procedures.
source: International Maritime Organization — London Protocol
status_note: Adopted in 2019 and available for provisional application by declaring Parties

document_title: Risk Assessment and Management Framework for CO2 Sequestration in Sub-seabed Geological Structures
notes: The framework establishes an overall risk-assessment and management process for subseabed CO2 storage, including stream characterization, site selection, impact hypotheses, monitoring, mitigation and long-term management. It supports national permitting review and does not approve a specific project or deployment.
source: International Maritime Organization — London Convention and Protocol
status_note: Adopted technical framework for use by London Protocol Parties

document_title: 2012 Specific Guidelines for the Assessment of Carbon Dioxide Streams for Disposal into Sub-seabed Geological Formations
notes: The guidelines elaborate national permitting and assessment procedures for subseabed geological storage, covering stream composition, site and storage-complex characterization, possible leakage pathways, monitoring, risk management and post-closure responsibility. They promote consistent review but do not replace project-specific decisions by competent authorities.
source: International Maritime Organization — London Convention and Protocol
status_note: Adopted in 2012 as specific assessment guidance

document_title: Directive 2009/31/EC on the Geological Storage of Carbon Dioxide
notes: The EU directive establishes a binding framework for geological CO2 storage within the Union, territorial seas, exclusive economic zones and continental shelves, requiring exploration and storage permits, site characterization, monitoring, corrective measures, closure and transfer of responsibility and prohibiting direct storage in the water column. Member States must implement it through domestic law and project-specific permits.
source: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
status_note: Directive in force and implemented through Member State legislation

document_title: Carbon Credits (Carbon Farming Initiative—Tidal Restoration of Blue Carbon Ecosystems) Methodology Determination 2022
notes: The Australian method sets eligibility, baselines, project boundaries, carbon pools, monitoring and abatement-calculation rules for tidal-restoration blue-carbon projects under the Australian Carbon Credit Unit scheme, enabling verified credits from restored tidal exchange. The method does not guarantee credit issuance; projects must still be registered, implemented and audited.
source: Australian Government — Federal Register of Legislation
status_note: Registered on 19 January 2022 and currently in force

document_title: Blue Carbon Conservation, Restoration and Accounting Program
notes: The Australian Government invested approximately AUD 30.6 million during 2021–2025 in domestic and international blue-carbon conservation, on-ground restoration, accounting tools and demonstrations covering coastal ecosystems such as mangroves, salt marshes and seagrass. The programme has ended, and its outputs may continue to be used, but the budget cannot be equated with achieved net removals.
source: Australian Government — Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
status_note: Programme operated from 2021 to 2025

document_title: Blue Carbon Ecosystem Restoration Grants
notes: During 2021–2025, funding supported multiple on-ground restoration projects in Australian blue-carbon ecosystems, including tidal-wetland hydrological restoration, seagrass and salt-marsh activities and partnerships with local and Indigenous communities. The funding period has ended, and actual carbon benefits must be assessed from project monitoring and accounting.
source: Australian Government — Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
status_note: Grant programme operated from 2021 to 2025

document_title: A Guide to Measuring and Accounting for the Benefits of Restoring Blue Carbon Ecosystems — Version 1
notes: The guidance provides methods and indicators for measuring ecological, carbon and co-benefits of blue-carbon restoration, supported by case studies. It improves consistency in project evaluation but is not a credit-issuance methodology and does not automatically demonstrate additional and permanent removals.
source: Australian Government — Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water
status_note: Version 1 published in 2024 and available for project use

document_title: Blue Carbon Promotion Strategy
notes: Korea's Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries proposed three strategic pillars: strengthening marine carbon uptake and climate-disaster response, expanding corporate, local and international participation, and promoting certification of emerging blue carbon while building a long-term implementation foundation. It is a comprehensive strategy covering restoration, research and certification directions, not evidence of completed international methodology recognition or issued credits.
source: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, Republic of Korea
status_note: National blue carbon strategy announced on 31 May 2023

document_title: Act on Carbon Dioxide Storage Businesses (Act No. 38 of 2024)
notes: Japan's CCS Business Act establishes licensing, prospecting and storage rights, safety oversight, operational duties and pipeline-transport rules for CO2 exploration and storage in seabed and other reservoirs. Promulgated in 2024, its main storage-business provisions took effect on 22 May 2026, creating a national legal basis for offshore geological storage; individual projects still require area designation and licences.
source: Government of Japan
status_note: Promulgated on 24 May 2024; principal storage-business provisions fully enforced from 22 May 2026

document_title: Cabinet Orders for Full Enforcement of the Act on Carbon Dioxide Storage Businesses
notes: The implementing order brought the principal CCS Business Act provisions into force on 22 May 2026 and established related transitional measures. It generally requires CO2 streams stored in marine reservoirs to have a concentration of at least 99%, while allowing regulatory exceptions where impurities pose limited marine-environment risk. The rule sets regulatory conditions and does not authorize a specific injection project.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan
status_note: Cabinet approved on 24 April 2026; full enforcement date 22 May 2026

document_title: Designation of a Sea Area Offshore Tomakomai as a Specified Area under the CCS Business Act
notes: Japan's Minister of Economy, Trade and Industry made the first designation under the CCS Business Act of part of the offshore area near Tomakomai, Hokkaido, as a specified area, enabling a public call for prospecting operators and subsequent licensing. The designation itself does not approve commercial storage or confirm achievable removal quantities.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan
status_note: Specified-area designation issued on 21 February 2025

document_title: Exploratory Drilling Permit for the Tomakomai Specified Area under the CCS Business Act
notes: Following regulatory review, consultation with the Hokkaido governor and stakeholder procedures, a prospecting licence was granted for the specified offshore Tomakomai area to investigate subseabed reservoir conditions. It covers exploration only and does not authorize commercial injection or permanent storage.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan
status_note: Exploratory drilling permit issued on 17 September 2025

document_title: Designation of a Sea Area Offshore Kujukuri as a Specified Area under the CCS Business Act
notes: Part of the offshore area near Kujukuri, Chiba Prefecture, was designated as a specified area under the CCS Business Act, establishing the legal spatial basis for a public call and licensing review of prospecting operators. It is a preliminary administrative decision and does not approve commercial CO2 injection.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan
status_note: Specified-area designation issued on 17 September 2025

document_title: Exploratory Drilling Permit for the Kujukuri Specified Area under the CCS Business Act
notes: After review against licensing criteria, consultation with the Chiba governor and stakeholder input, Metropolitan Area CCS Company was authorized to undertake prospecting in the specified offshore Kujukuri area. The decision authorizes exploratory drilling only; storage operations require separate licensing and environmental-safety review.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japan
status_note: Exploratory drilling permit issued on 15 April 2026

document_title: FY2024 Advanced CCS Projects
notes: Under a Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry programme, JOGMEC selected nine advanced CCS projects to develop replicable business models and domestic and international transport-and-storage chains, including several offshore or subseabed storage options. Selection provides policy and early-stage project support and does not replace prospecting or storage licences under the CCS Business Act.
source: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry / JOGMEC, Japan
status_note: Nine projects selected for FY2024 advanced CCS development

subnational_area: UK territorial sea and Gas Importation and Storage Zone
document_title: Energy Act 2008 — Part 1, Chapter 3: Storage of Carbon Dioxide
notes: The UK Energy Act 2008 establishes the statutory licensing system for offshore CO2 storage in territorial waters and designated gas-importation and storage zones and empowers authorities to issue, condition, transfer and revoke storage licences. It is the foundational framework; individual reservoirs require separate approval.
source: UK Parliament
status_note: Statutory offshore carbon dioxide storage licensing framework in force

subnational_area: UK territorial sea and Gas Importation and Storage Zone
document_title: Storage of Carbon Dioxide (Licensing etc.) Regulations 2010
notes: The UK regulations implement the EU geological-storage directive and detail offshore exploration and storage licensing, site selection, monitoring, corrective measures, closure, transfer of responsibility and financial-security requirements. In force since October 2010, they impose binding conditions but do not automatically grant a site licence.
source: UK Government
status_note: Regulations in force from 1 October 2010, as amended

subnational_area: UK Continental Shelf areas offered in the first offshore carbon storage licensing round
document_title: 1st Offshore Carbon Dioxide Storage Licensing Round Appropriate Assessment
notes: An appropriate assessment and public consultation were conducted for the first UK offshore CO2-storage licensing round to identify risks to protected marine sites and species and inform licensing decisions. The assessment process is complete, but its conclusions are not themselves storage licences.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero / OPRED
status_note: Assessment and consultation completed; outcome published in May 2023

subnational_area: UK Continental Shelf areas offered in the second offshore carbon storage licensing round
document_title: 2nd Offshore Carbon Dioxide Storage Licensing Round Appropriate Assessment
notes: The second offshore CO2-storage licensing round is subject to habitats appropriate assessment and public consultation on possible effects on European marine protected sites. The process remains under assessment and decision formation and cannot be treated as granted storage licences.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero / OPRED
status_note: Consultation published on 20 July 2026; licensing decisions remain under assessment

subnational_area: Southern North Sea / East Coast Cluster
document_title: Carbon Dioxide Transport and Storage Licence — Net Zero North Sea Storage Limited
notes: A CO2 transport and storage economic licence was granted to Net Zero North Sea Storage Limited under the Energy Act 2023 and took effect on 10 December 2024. It regulates network operation, while seabed reservoir development, injection and environmental approvals remain subject to other licences and conditions.
source: UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
status_note: Transport and storage licence entered into force on 10 December 2024

document_title: Carbon Dioxide Transport and Storage Licence — Liverpool Bay CCS Limited
notes: A CO2 transport and storage economic licence was granted to Liverpool Bay CCS Limited under the Energy Act 2023 to support operation of the Liverpool Bay network. It is an operating licence and should not be confused with a seabed injection permit, environmental approval or achieved permanent-storage quantity.
source: UK Secretary of State for Energy Security and Net Zero
status_note: Transport and storage licence awarded on 22 April 2025

document_title: Energy Act 2023 — Carbon Dioxide Transport and Storage Licensing Regime
notes: The Energy Act 2023 establishes an economic-licensing regime for CO2 transport and storage networks, prohibits unlicensed pipeline transport or geological-storage-facility operation and regulates licences, exemptions, oversight and changes of control. It operates alongside offshore site licensing under the Energy Act 2008 and mainly regulates network business rather than replacing environmental permits.
source: UK Parliament
status_note: Statutory economic licensing regime in force

document_title: Offshore Energy Strategic Environmental Assessment 5 Scoping Consultation
notes: The consultation defines the scope of a strategic environmental assessment for future UK offshore leasing and licensing plans covering renewable energy, natural gas, CO2 and hydrogen storage. It includes cumulative effects and alternatives for offshore CO2 storage at policy level but is only a scoping consultation and does not license any block.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero / OPRED
status_note: Scoping consultation opened on 29 January 2026

subnational_area: Norwegian Continental Shelf / Øygarden–North Sea chain
document_title: Longship — Carbon Capture and Storage (Meld. St. 33 (2019–2020))
notes: The Norwegian government submitted the Longship full-chain CCS project to Parliament, covering industrial capture, shipping to the Øygarden terminal and pipeline injection into geological formations beneath the North Sea, with state funding and risk sharing. The project is operational, but budgeted and designed capacity in the white paper is not the same as actual annual storage.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Petroleum and Energy
status_note: White paper submitted in 2020; Longship and Northern Lights implementation remains active

subnational_area: Aurora storage complex, Norwegian North Sea
document_title: Northern Lights Exploitation Licence 001 for CO2 Storage
notes: The Norwegian government awarded Northern Lights the first development licence, EL001, for subseabed CO2 storage, providing a statutory basis for development, injection and long-term monitoring of the Aurora reservoir. It is a project-level authorization; actual injection remains constrained by the development plan, infrastructure capacity and continuing regulation.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Petroleum and Energy
status_note: First Norwegian exploitation licence for CO2 storage awarded on 11 January 2019

document_title: Approval of the Northern Lights Phase 2 Development Plan
notes: Norway's Ministry of Energy approved the Northern Lights phase-two development plan, increasing transport and storage capacity from 1.5 million to at least 5 million tonnes per year. The approval supports expansion of the existing North Sea project, but design capacity is not achieved annual net storage.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Energy
status_note: Phase 2 development plan approved on 17 June 2025

subnational_area: Northern Lights transport, receiving and offshore storage facilities
document_title: Completion Confirmation for Northern Lights Transport and Storage Facilities
notes: Under the state-aid agreement, Norway's Ministry of Energy confirmed completion and entry into operation of Northern Lights transport, reception, injection and storage facilities, marking the transition from construction to operation. This project-management confirmation does not replace continuing monitoring, reporting and safety obligations under the storage licence.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Energy
status_note: Completion confirmation issued on 1 October 2025; facilities in operational phase

document_title: First Three Exclusive Offshore CO2 Storage Exploration Licences in the Danish North Sea
notes: Denmark awarded the first three North Sea offshore CO2-storage exploration licences to TotalEnergies and to consortia involving INEOS and Wintershall Dea to assess potential full-scale reservoir development. The licences initiate exploration and work programmes and do not approve commercial injection or determine final capacity.
source: Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities / Danish Energy Agency
status_note: Three exclusive offshore exploration licences awarded in February 2023

subnational_area: Nini West field, Danish North Sea
document_title: Permit for the Project Greensand Nini West CO2 Storage Demonstration
notes: The Danish Energy Agency authorized Project Greensand to inject and store up to approximately 15,000 tonnes of CO2 on a test basis in the depleted Nini West oil field to validate cross-border transport and long-term subseabed storage. Demonstration injection took place in 2023; the limited permit is not full-scale commercial authorization.
source: Danish Energy Agency
status_note: Demonstration permit issued in 2022; limited injection demonstration conducted in 2023

subnational_area: Nini A / Nini West, Danish North Sea
document_title: Approval of the Nini West Storage Plan and Permission for Full-scale CO2 Storage
notes: The Danish Energy Agency approved the Nini West storage plan and its use as Denmark's first full-scale CO2-storage project, moving the project from demonstration toward commercial storage. Approval remains subject to environmental, monitoring and operational conditions, and approved capacity is not the amount already injected or permanently stored.
source: Danish Energy Agency
status_note: First Danish full-scale CO2 storage approval issued on 18 December 2025

document_title: Norway–France Administrative Arrangement on Cross-border Transportation of CO2 for Permanent Geological Storage
notes: France and Norway established an administrative arrangement for cross-border transport of CO2 from France for permanent geological storage in Norway and required consistency with the London Protocol and EU emissions-trading and storage rules. It creates an institutional pathway for cooperation, while individual transport, injection and liability matters require national permits and commercial agreements.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Energy / Government of France
status_note: Administrative arrangement signed on 23 June 2025

document_title: Norway–Belgium Agreement to Enable Cross-border CO2 Pipeline Transport and Storage
notes: Belgium and Norway signed a bilateral agreement establishing a cooperation basis for pipeline transport of CO2 from Belgium to permanent geological storage on the Norwegian continental shelf and supporting European cross-border CCS infrastructure. It does not directly approve a particular pipeline or reservoir; national regulation, offshore permits and investment decisions remain necessary.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Energy / Government of Belgium
status_note: Bilateral agreement signed on 26 March 2026

document_title: Finland–Norway Memorandum of Understanding on Cross-border CO2 Transport for Permanent Geological Storage
notes: Finland and Norway signed a memorandum of understanding to advance cross-border transport of captured Finnish CO2 for permanent geological storage in Norway in line with existing international legal frameworks. It is primarily policy coordination and is not a project permit or guaranteed storage commitment.
source: Ministry of the Environment of Finland / Norwegian Ministry of Energy
status_note: Memorandum of Understanding signed on 4 September 2025

document_title: Norway–Netherlands Memorandum of Understanding on Cross-border Transport and Storage of CO2
notes: Norway and the Netherlands signed a memorandum of understanding to coordinate regulatory and cooperative arrangements for cross-border transport and permanent subseabed storage in Norway of Dutch-origin CO2. It provides a policy basis for later projects and interstate arrangements but does not replace transport, reservoir or environmental permits.
source: Norwegian Ministry of Energy / Netherlands Ministry for Climate and Energy Policy
status_note: Memorandum of Understanding signed on 15 April 2024

document_title: Norway–Switzerland Agreement on CCUS, Carbon Dioxide Removal and Cross-border Permanent Storage
notes: The Norway–Switzerland agreement establishes a legal framework for cooperation on CCUS, carbon dioxide removal, cross-border transport and permanent geological storage in Norway and addresses transfers of mitigation outcomes under Paris Agreement Article 6. It supports cross-border value chains and accounting cooperation, while specific storage projects require permits and mitigation outcomes require subsequent accounting and authorization.
source: Governments of Norway and Switzerland
status_note: Bilateral agreement signed on 17 June 2025

document_title: RETAKE — CO2 Removal by Alkalinity Enhancement: Potential, Benefits and Risks
notes: The CDRmare RETAKE consortium systematically assesses the removal potential, feasibility, ecological side effects, cost, social implications and monitoring and accounting of ocean alkalinity enhancement through laboratory work, mesocosms and modelling. It remains research and assessment and does not authorize large-scale alkalinity addition in Germany.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / RETAKE Consortium
status_note: Funded since 2021; Phase II research continues through 2027

document_title: ASMASYS — Assessing Marine Carbon Removal: Synthesis, Scenarios and Governance
notes: ASMASYS develops an integrated marine-CDR assessment framework and German implementation scenarios comparing technical potential, environmental effects, governance, justice, public acceptance and desirability and synthesizing results from CDRmare technology projects. It produces assessment tools and policy evidence and does not deploy negative-emissions engineering.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / ASMASYS Consortium
status_note: Funded since 2021; Phase II assessment work continues from 2024 to 2027

subnational_area: German North Sea and Baltic coasts, with international comparison sites
document_title: sea4soCiety — Innovative Approaches to Improving the Carbon Storage Potential of Vegetated Coastal Ecosystems
notes: Sea4soCiety quantifies carbon stocks, stability and greenhouse-gas trade-offs in vegetated coastal ecosystems such as salt marshes, seagrass and mangroves, uses remote sensing to identify potential expansion zones and studies governance, social acceptance and policy roadmaps. It identifies possible areas and designs but remains research and assessment rather than implemented large-scale restoration.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / sea4soCiety Consortium
status_note: Funded since 2021; Phase II research continues through 2027

document_title: GEOSTOR — Submarine Carbon Dioxide Storage in Geological Formations of the German North Sea
notes: GEOSTOR assesses storage capacity, site suitability, leakage risk, environmental effects, monitoring and marine-spatial-use conflicts for geological formations beneath the German North Sea to inform possible million-tonne-scale storage. It does not conduct commercial injection or constitute a German offshore storage permit.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / GEOSTOR Consortium
status_note: Funded since 2021; Phase II research continues through 2027

document_title: Test-ArtUp — Road Testing Ocean Artificial Upwelling
notes: Test-ArtUp used prototypes, field trials and ecological, economic and legal analysis to assess artificial upwelling feasibility, removal potential, cost effectiveness and governance and compare it with other marine negative-emissions technologies. The project concluded at the end of 2024, and its results are research validation rather than continuing deployment authorization.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / Test-ArtUp Consortium
status_note: Research consortium funded from 2021 and completed at the end of 2024

subnational_area: Reykjanes Ridge and offshore CCS monitoring test sites
document_title: AIMS3 — Alternate Scenarios, Innovative Technologies and Monitoring Approaches for Sub-seabed Storage of Carbon Dioxide
notes: AIMS3 studies the feasibility of storing CO2 in basaltic crust at mid-ocean ridges, develops low-cost leakage detection and quantitative monitoring tools and plans controlled injection demonstrations and best-practice recommendations. It is phased research and not a commercial subseabed-injection permit; any experiment remains subject to research and environmental approvals.
source: German Marine Research Alliance — CDRmare / AIMS3 Consortium
status_note: Funded since 2021; Phase II work continues through 2027

document_title: Carbon-Negative Hydrogen Production Countering the Effects of Ocean Acidification — Phase 1
notes: Phase one of the UK greenhouse-gas-removal innovation programme funded Planetary Hydrogen to develop an electrochemical process combining renewable hydrogen production with OAE and to create analytical and numerical tools and an engineering design for a one-tonne-per-day CO2 test unit. The completed phase produced feasibility work and test design, not an ocean-discharge permit or proof of durable net removal.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (formerly BEIS)
status_note: Phase 1 project selected in 2021; feasibility work completed and a final report is available

document_title: SeaCURE Direct Ocean Capture Demonstration — Phase 2
notes: The UK Government provided approximately GBP 3 million to the University of Exeter for phase two of SeaCURE, a demonstration system for direct CO2 removal from seawater. Official information states that it can remove more than 90% of CO2 from treated water, allowing discharged low-carbon water to reabsorb atmospheric CO2. The project has produced a final report, but demonstration results are not commercial-scale deployment authorization or a substitute for full life-cycle verification.
source: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
status_note: Phase 2 demonstration funded in 2022; project completed and final report published

document_title: Biological Influence on Future Ocean Storage of Carbon (BIO-Carbon) Programme
notes: The UK Natural Environment Research Council established the BIO-Carbon programme, investing approximately GBP 10.3 million in several rounds during 2022–2027 to study how marine biological processes affect future ocean carbon storage and improve global predictions, with attention to international waters and carbon policy. It builds scientific evidence and models and is neither a blue-carbon credit methodology nor authorization for engineering.
source: UK Research and Innovation — Natural Environment Research Council
status_note: Multi-round NERC research programme running from 2022 to 2027

document_title: Biological Influence on Ocean Carbon: Novel Modelling Approaches — UKRI–NASA Funding Opportunity
notes: UKRI and NASA issued a joint 2026 call to translate key biological controls on ocean carbon storage into new global model representations, with GBP 1 million available on the UK side. The call closed on 14 July 2026 and selected projects are expected to begin in January 2027; at the time of entry, it remained under review and was not an active funded project or policy conclusion.
source: UK Research and Innovation — NERC / NASA
status_note: Call closed on 14 July 2026; award decisions were not yet confirmed as of 5 August 2026

document_title: Multiple-Model Assessment of Biological Influence on Ocean Carbon — UKRI–NASA Funding Opportunity
notes: UKRI and NASA issued a GBP 625,000 joint 2026 call for multi-model assessment of how ocean biological processes influence carbon storage and uncertainty through 2100, linking BIO-Carbon and NASA EXPORTS data. The call has closed but awards were not confirmed at the time of entry, so it is classified as under review rather than active research.
source: UK Research and Innovation — NERC / NASA
status_note: Call closed on 14 July 2026; successful projects are intended to start in January 2027

subnational_area: European coastal seagrass and salt-marsh systems
document_title: SeaSym — Symbioses Between Plants and Sulfur-Oxidizing Bacteria Sustain Coastal Blue-Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The ERC-funded SeaSym project studies the diversity, function and dispersal of sulfur-oxidizing bacteria in the roots of seagrass and salt-marsh plants and their role in elemental cycling and blue-carbon ecosystem health. With approximately EUR 2 million for 2025–2029, it is basic mechanism research, not restoration and not quantified additional removal.
source: European Commission — European Research Council / CORDIS
status_note: Grant agreement signed in 2024; project active from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029

subnational_area: Arctic, sub-Arctic and other emerging polar marine ecosystems
document_title: SEA-Quester — Blue-Carbon Production, Export and Sequestration in Emerging Polar Ecosystems
notes: The EU SEA-Quester project uses polar field surveys, process experiments and modelling to assess blue-carbon production, export, storage and uncertainty in emerging coastal, pelagic and benthic ecosystems and develop foundations for appropriate accounting. Running from 2024 to 2028, it remains research assessment and does not authorize polar sink enhancement or establish verified removals.
source: European Commission — Horizon Europe / CORDIS
status_note: Grant agreement signed in 2023; project active from 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028

subnational_area: Canadian salt marshes, seagrass meadows, macroalgae beds and coastal sediments
document_title: Report on Evaluating Blue Carbon as an Effective Climate Mitigation Strategy for Canada
notes: A Fisheries and Oceans Canada blue-carbon working group assessed potential contributions of protection, restoration and expansion of blue-carbon ecosystems to national climate goals and summarized evidence, limitations and key knowledge gaps across habitats and regions. The report states that available data are insufficient to quantify Canada's mitigation benefit, so it informs research and policy rather than setting engineering targets or a credit methodology.
source: Fisheries and Oceans Canada
status_note: Official assessment published in 2025 and retained as a basis for future research and policy development

subnational_area: Dartmouth, Nova Scotia; municipal-wastewater proof-of-concept context
document_title: Unlocking New Potential in Wastewater Treatment — Ocean Carbon Removal Proof of Concept
notes: Canada's National Research Council IRAP awarded CAD 75,000 to Planetary Technologies to integrate alkalinity extraction and marine carbon removal with wastewater engineering and conduct a safe, community-engaged proof of concept using municipal fly ash. The agreement runs through 31 August 2026; it remains R&D validation and is not an environmental permit for continuing alkalinity addition to the ocean.
source: National Research Council Canada — Industrial Research Assistance Program
status_note: Contribution agreement active from 1 April 2025 to 31 August 2026

document_title: Halifax Harbour Living Laboratory for Ocean OAE-CDR and Artificial Reoxygenation — NSERC Ship-Time Grant
notes: Canada's NSERC 2026 Ship Time programme awarded CAD 98,670 to a Dalhousie University project using Halifax Harbour as an offshore research platform for climate-mitigation technologies such as OAE and artificial reoxygenation. The one-year funding supports investigation and trial conditions and does not authorize routine OAE deployment or certify performance.
source: Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada
status_note: One-year Ship Time award announced in 2026

document_title: Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
notes: Australia and IUCN implemented the Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund during 2021–2025, providing project-preparation and implementation finance for blue-carbon protection and restoration in developing countries and supporting a portfolio of 12 credible, investment-ready projects. The fund has ended; project preparation or use of credit finance does not mean the fund created a uniform credit-issuance system.
source: Australian Government — Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water / IUCN
status_note: Funding partnership operated from 2021 to 2025 and delivered 12 readiness or implementation projects

subnational_area: Global partnership of governments, NGOs, intergovernmental bodies and research institutions
document_title: International Partnership for Blue Carbon
notes: The International Partnership for Blue Carbon was launched in 2015 and connects government agencies, NGOs, international organizations and research bodies to improve conservation, restoration and management through knowledge exchange, cooperation and action and to support national policy and projects. It is an international coordination and capacity-building mechanism, not a binding treaty or credit issuer.
source: International Partnership for Blue Carbon / Australian Government DCCEEW
status_note: International partnership launched in 2015 and remains active

subnational_area: Papua New Guinea, Fiji and wider Pacific capacity-building context
document_title: Pacific Blue Carbon Program
notes: The Australia-supported Pacific Blue Carbon programme strengthened national climate action in Pacific island countries through mapping, measurement and accounting during 2018–2024, with particular work in Papua New Guinea and Fiji on the feasibility of blue-carbon offsets and biodiversity and livelihood co-benefits. The project has ended; its work was capacity building and investment preparation rather than issued offsets.
source: Australian Government / Pacific regional partners
status_note: Regional programme operated from 2018 to 2024

subnational_area: Japanese marine research and controlled technology-development sites
document_title: Development of Nature-Positive Ocean-Based Negative Emission Technologies — CREST JPMJCR25J1
notes: The JST CREST project studies electrochemical direct ocean capture and ocean alkalinity enhancement and develops a neutral comparison method incorporating advanced environmental-impact assessment to advance nature-positive ocean negative-emissions technologies. Running from 2025 to 2030, it remains technology research and evaluation and does not authorize commercial ocean discharge or capture.
source: Japan Science and Technology Agency — CREST / J-GLOBAL
status_note: CREST project JPMJCR25J1 active from 2025 to 2030

subnational_area: Continental-slope and offshore waters connecting land, coasts and the open ocean
document_title: Carbon Dynamics and Sequestration of Offshore Blue Carbon — CREST JPMJCR25J2
notes: This JST CREST project combines innovative ocean observations, sediment analysis, marine-ecosystem models and near-bed particle-transport models to quantify offshore blue-carbon sequestration from the surface to the seabed in areas such as continental slopes. Running from 2025 to 2030, it aims to provide a scientific basis for broad-area management and use and is not an implemented sink-enhancement project.
source: Japan Science and Technology Agency — CREST / J-GLOBAL
status_note: CREST project JPMJCR25J2 active from 2025 to 2030

document_title: Innovating Ocean Models Through Discovery of Hidden Microbial Carbon Flow — CREST JPMJCR25J3
notes: This JST CREST project studies how organic molecules released by phytoplankton in oligotrophic waters affect microbial activity, elemental composition and long-term carbon storage and uses cruises and experiments to build a new marine carbon-cycle model incorporating microbial carbon flows. Running from 2025 to 2030, it is mechanism and modelling research rather than engineering deployment.
source: Japan Science and Technology Agency — CREST / J-GLOBAL
status_note: CREST project JPMJCR25J3 active from 2025 to 2030

document_title: Marine Storage of Humic-Like Fluorescent Dissolved Organic Matter: Quantitative Assessment and Future Projections — CREST JPMJCR25J4
notes: This JST CREST project focuses on highly refractory humic-like fluorescent dissolved organic matter produced by marine microbes, develops methods to convert fluorescence intensity to carbon concentration, and combines broad observations and biogeochemical models to quantify global production fluxes and changes under warming. Running from 2025 to 2030, it is microbial-carbon-pump mechanism and monitoring research.
source: Japan Science and Technology Agency — CREST / J-GLOBAL
status_note: CREST project JPMJCR25J4 active from 2025 to 2030

subnational_area: Japan and twelve participating European countries
document_title: EIG CONCERT-Japan Oceans: Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation — 2026 Selected Projects
notes: JST and funding agencies from twelve European countries selected six three-year projects from the 2025 Oceans: Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation joint call, covering blue-carbon technologies, marine ecosystem protection and analysis of ocean processes, with cooperation during 2026–2028. The decision confirms research funding and does not approve blue-carbon engineering or validate removal quantities.
source: Japan Science and Technology Agency / EIG CONCERT-Japan
status_note: Six projects selected on 28 January 2026 for cooperation during FY2026–FY2028

subnational_area: Japanese ports, coasts, seagrass and tidal-flat monitoring areas
document_title: Green-Laser Blue-Carbon Data Measurement Manual — Version 1
notes: Japan's Ports and Harbours Bureau and the Port and Airport Research Institute issued a green-laser blue-carbon measurement manual establishing measurement criteria and precautions for accurately identifying the distribution and area of seaweed beds, tidal flats and other blue-carbon ecosystems using green lasers with high underwater transmission. It can support CO2-uptake calculations but is non-binding guidance and not itself the J-Blue Credit verification methodology.
source: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan
status_note: Version 1 announced on 31 March 2026
