document_title: Blue Carbon Data Archive System (BDAS) — Public WebGIS Launch
notes: Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism and the Port and Airport Research Institute launched BDAS, combining remote-sensing data such as green-laser drones with bathymetry, substrate, water temperature and transparency to estimate seaweed-bed distribution and area through numerical models and publish results in a WebGIS. It can support uptake calculations, but some upload functions remain phased and it does not automatically verify credits or restoration performance.
source: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan
status_note: Public WebGIS use launched on 5 June 2026; additional upload functions were still being completed

document_title: FY2025 J-Blue Credit Certification Decisions — 52 Projects
notes: Japan's Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism confirmed that JBE, the accredited administrator, certified and issued J-Blue Credits in fiscal year 2025 for 52 projects generating CO2 uptake through protection, restoration and creation of seaweed beds, tidal flats and similar habitats. This record covers the annual certification outcome rather than duplicating the scheme itself; the number of certifications is not equivalent to permanent net removal by all projects and remains subject to project-specific monitoring and boundaries.
source: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan / Japan Blue Economy Association
status_note: Fifty-two FY2025 project certifications announced on 17 March 2026

document_title: 国家标准计划20232569-T-418《典型蓝碳生态系统碳汇监测与核算技术规范》
notes: The proposed Chinese national standard would unify technical requirements for monitoring and accounting of carbon sinks in representative blue-carbon ecosystems under the National Marine Standardization Technical Committee and the Ministry of Natural Resources. The plan was issued in 2023 and remained pending approval as of August 2026; it is not yet an effective national standard and cannot be used for compliance verification.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / National Standard Information Public Service Platform
status_note: National standard plan issued on 29 December 2023 and shown as under approval in August 2026

document_title: 国家标准计划20232568-T-418《典型蓝碳生态系统碳储量调查与评估技术规范》
notes: The proposed Chinese national standard would establish uniform methods for surveying and assessing carbon stocks in representative blue-carbon ecosystems under the National Marine Standardization Technical Committee and the Ministry of Natural Resources. The plan was issued in 2023 and remained pending approval as of August 2026, so it cannot yet be used as an effective accounting or certification standard.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / National Standard Information Public Service Platform
status_note: National standard plan issued on 29 December 2023 and shown as under approval in August 2026

document_title: DB21/T 4422-2026《海草床碳库调查技术规程》
notes: Liaoning's recommended local standard specifies technical procedures and requirements for surveying carbon pools in seagrass beds. Managed by the provincial natural-resources department, it was published on 7 May 2026 and took effect on 7 June. It supports consistent carbon-stock surveys and is not a restoration project, credit-issuance rule or additional-removal target.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / Liaoning Provincial Market Regulation Administration
status_note: Recommended local standard published on 7 May 2026 and effective from 7 June 2026

document_title: DB44/T 2607.1-2025《滨海蓝碳碳汇能力调查与核算技术指南 第1部分：通则》
notes: Guangdong's recommended local standard establishes general principles, boundaries and a technical framework for surveying and accounting the sink capacity of coastal blue-carbon ecosystems across the province. Published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April, it improves consistency but does not create a crediting system or demonstrate additional removals.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / Guangdong Provincial Market Regulation Administration
status_note: Recommended local standard published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April 2025

document_title: DB44/T 2607.2-2025《滨海蓝碳碳汇能力调查与核算技术指南 第2部分：红树林》
notes: Guangdong's recommended local standard specifies survey and accounting requirements for mangrove ecosystem carbon-sink capacity within the province and took effect on 23 April 2025. It is a technical accounting standard, not a mangrove-restoration programme or credit-issuance decision.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / Guangdong Provincial Market Regulation Administration
status_note: Recommended local standard published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April 2025

document_title: DB44/T 2607.3-2025《滨海蓝碳碳汇能力调查与核算技术指南 第3部分：海草床》
notes: Guangdong's recommended local standard specifies survey and accounting requirements for seagrass ecosystem carbon-sink capacity. Published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April, it provides a technical basis but does not mean restoration has occurred or automatically generate tradable credits.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / Guangdong Provincial Market Regulation Administration
status_note: Recommended local standard published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April 2025

document_title: DB44/T 2607.4-2025《滨海蓝碳碳汇能力调查与核算技术指南 第4部分：盐沼》
notes: Guangdong's recommended local standard specifies survey and accounting requirements for salt-marsh ecosystem carbon-sink capacity and took effect on 23 April 2025. It is local technical guidance, not a restoration project, mandatory regulatory requirement or credit-issuance mechanism.
source: State Administration for Market Regulation / Guangdong Provincial Market Regulation Administration
status_note: Recommended local standard published on 23 January 2025 and effective from 23 April 2025

subnational_area: Northeast Pacific and Northeast Atlantic open-ocean deployments
document_title: NASA EXport Processes in the Ocean from RemoTe Sensing (EXPORTS) Field Campaign
notes: NASA's multi-year EXPORTS field programme used research vessels, autonomous underwater vehicles, floats and remote sensing to study the export and fate of organic carbon produced in the upper ocean and its role in the Earth carbon cycle, with Pacific and Atlantic deployments in 2018 and 2021. The completed programme was biological-carbon-pump observation and modelling, not ocean negative-emissions engineering.
source: National Aeronautics and Space Administration — Earth Science
status_note: Field deployments completed in 2018 and 2021; campaign study period ended in 2021

document_title: Carbon Capture and Ocean Acidification Mitigation Potential by Seaweed Farms in Tropical and Subtropical Coastal Environments
notes: A NOPP-funded project uses sensors and numerical models at three operating seaweed farms in Florida and Okinawa, Japan, to assess carbon capture, ocean-acidification mitigation and ecological risks from seaweed aquaculture. It is research assessment and does not establish verified durable removal or authorize expanded sinking or credit issuance.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; research project, not deployment authorization

document_title: Assessing the Chemical and Biological Implications of Alkalinity Enhancement Using Carbonate Salts from Captured Carbon Dioxide to Mitigate Ocean Acidification and Enable mCDR
notes: The project develops and tests a pilot system converting captured CO2 into sodium carbonate and bicarbonate and studies mineral precipitation, chemical quality control and biological responses when these salts are used for OAE. It remains technology and ecological-safety research and has not produced commercial deployment authorization or verified removals.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; pilot-scale research completed/ending, no deployment authorization

document_title: Electrolysis-Driven Weathering of Basic Minerals for Long-Term Ocean Buffering and CO2 Reduction
notes: The project studies electrolysis and alkaline-mineral weathering to increase seawater buffering capacity and uses experiments and models to assess the risks, constraints and potential benefits of OAE while informing a regulatory strategy roadmap. Its primary function is research and proof of concept, not permission for large-scale ocean addition.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active research and proof-of-concept work

subnational_area: Atlantic and United States coastal research settings
document_title: Determining the Influence of Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement on Foraminifera Calcification, Distribution, and Calcium Carbonate Production
notes: The project assesses effects of OAE materials on foraminiferal calcification, distribution and calcium-carbonate production to determine whether biological calcification reduces removal efficiency or creates ecological risk. It is experimental mechanism research and does not authorize ocean release of alkaline materials.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active biological-response research

document_title: Assessing Efficacy of Electrochemical Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement at an Existing Outfall Using Tracer Release Experiments and Oceanographic Models
notes: Using a San Francisco Bay wastewater-treatment outfall, the project designs an electrochemical alkalinity-enhancement experiment with tracers, numerical models and environmental sampling to assess uptake efficiency, dispersion and impacts. It is a controlled research trial and method validation, not approval for routine outfall alkalinization.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; field-research funding period ended, not continuing discharge authorization

document_title: Engaging U.S. Commercial Fishing Community to Develop Recommendations for Fishery-Sensitive mCDR Governance, Collaborative Research and Monitoring, and Outreach to Fishing Communities
notes: Through engagement with commercial fishing communities, the project develops fisheries-sensitive recommendations for marine-CDR governance, co-research, monitoring and communication and identifies possible conflicts, social effects and participation mechanisms. Its outputs are governance research and advice, not deployment approval for a specific technology.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; participatory governance research funding period ended

document_title: Coupling Desalination with Novel mCDR Membranes
notes: The project develops functional materials that can be attached to existing seawater-desalination membranes to release CO2 from seawater in coordination with desalination and includes prototyping, modelling and techno-economic assessment. It establishes a technical foundation for direct ocean capture but does not authorize a commercial marine capture facility.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; research and prototyping period ended

document_title: Biotic Calcification Impacts on Marine Carbon Dioxide Removal Additionality
notes: The project uses ocean models to assess biologically induced calcification and associated CO2 release under OAE and quantify uncertain effects on long-term efficiency, additionality and potential credit value. The research can inform future MRV but does not establish a crediting methodology.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active modelling research

document_title: Tidal Wetlands as a Low-pH Environment for Accelerated and Scalable Olivine Dissolution
notes: The project studies whether low-pH tidal-wetland environments can accelerate olivine dissolution and assesses the scalability, removal efficiency and ecological risks of enhanced weathering and OAE. It is a four-year research project and not large-scale mineral application in wetlands.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active four-year research project

subnational_area: Southern Ocean, Equatorial Pacific and Northeast Pacific
document_title: Multiscale Observing System Simulation Experiments for Iron Fertilization in the Southern Ocean, Equatorial Pacific, and Northeast Pacific
notes: The project conducts observing-system simulation experiments with high-resolution and global biogeochemical models to evaluate the effectiveness, long-term effects, ecological disturbance and monitoring configurations needed for possible future ocean iron-fertilization trials. It neither conducts nor authorizes actual fertilization.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; modelling programme ended, no ocean-fertilization authorization

subnational_area: Potential mCDR deployment regions in United States waters
document_title: Data Requirements for Quantifying Natural Variability and the Background Ocean Carbon Sink in mCDR Models
notes: The project defines data needs for air–sea CO2 fluxes, the background ocean sink and natural variability and develops machine-learning and model benchmarks to distinguish additional marine-CDR removal and support future MRV. It builds evidence but does not issue credits or prescribe a uniform accounting method.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; three-year modelling and observing assessment ended

subnational_area: Pacific tropical and subtropical coral reefs
document_title: Assessing the Effects and Risks of Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement on the Physiology, Functionality, Calcification, and Mineralogy of Corals and Crustose Coralline Algae in the Pacific
notes: The project uses laboratory and mesocosm experiments to assess acute and chronic effects of quicklime, sodium hydroxide and olivine on physiology, calcification and mineral composition of Pacific corals and coralline algae and identify safe operating conditions. It is ecological-risk research and not an OAE permit for coral-reef areas.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active ecological-risk research

document_title: Assessing Carbon Dioxide Removal and Ecosystem Response for an Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement Field Trial
notes: The project equips a Gulf of Maine alkalinity-enhancement field trial with gliders, pH and dye sensors to measure additional carbon uptake, dispersion, leakage and ecosystem responses and provide data for future MRV practice. It is controlled research and monitoring support, not commercial-scale OAE authorization.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; funded field-trial assessment period ended

subnational_area: Coastal lagoon adjacent to a golf course
document_title: An Opportunity to Study Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement, Carbon Dioxide Removal, and Ecosystem Impacts Through Coastal Liming
notes: The project observes a coastal golf course where lime is routinely applied and monitors inorganic carbon, total alkalinity and ecological changes in a nearby lagoon before and after application to study how land-based alkaline inputs affect nearshore carbon removal. It uses an existing land-management practice and is not a new ocean-discharge permit.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active coastal field research

subnational_area: Atlantic research cruises and OAE plume field trial
document_title: Assessing the Laboratory and Field Responses of Diatoms and Coccolithophores to Ocean Alkalinity Enhancement
notes: Through laboratory work, research cruises and field observation of alkalinity plumes, the project assesses productivity, physiology and carbon-export responses of diatoms, coccolithophores and natural microbial communities to OAE. It identifies ecological effects and efficiency changes and does not authorize continuing alkaline addition.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active laboratory and field research

document_title: Developing a Coupled Benthic-Pelagic Biogeochemical Model to Evaluate the Effectiveness of mCDR Interventions
notes: The project develops coupled benthic–water-column biogeochemical models to simulate carbon and nutrient exchange and storage in sediments and assess permanence, additionality and verifiability of seaweed farming and benthic ecological restoration. It is modelling and evidence building and does not implement a specific project.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2026; active four-year model-development project

document_title: Quantifying the Efficacy of Wastewater Alkalinity Enhancement on mCDR and Acidification Mitigation in a Large Estuary
notes: The project assesses carbon-removal efficiency, cost and environmental and biological effects of wastewater-effluent alkalinization in Chesapeake Bay using existing dosing and discharge infrastructure. Although some discharge activities operate under conventional permits, the project is feasibility research and not authorization for scaled effluent alkalinization for marine CDR.
source: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / National Oceanographic Partnership Program (NOPP)
status_note: Fiscal years funded: 2023–2025; three-year feasibility research period ended

subnational_area: Ireland, Canada, Germany, Malta, Norway, Poland and Greece
document_title: JPI Oceans Joint Call on Blue Carbon Ecosystems
notes: The JPI Oceans joint call involves several countries and funds improved scientific knowledge, measurement methods and protocols for blue-carbon ecosystems and identification of effective interventions for mitigation and adaptation. It is a multinational research-funding mechanism, not adoption of a uniform accounting standard or implementation of a particular restoration project.
source: JPI Oceans / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Call opened 4 November 2025; programme horizon extends to 2029

subnational_area: Indian Ocean, South Atlantic and South Pacific project pipeline
document_title: Blue Catalyst Fund
notes: The fund uses recoverable early-stage finance, technical assistance and transaction support to reduce risk as high-integrity blue-carbon projects move from concept to investment and requires community participation, inclusion and measurable social benefits. Its main function is finance and project preparation, not verification, credit issuance or achieved quantified removals.
source: Fair Carbon / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Started 1 November 2025; planned through 2035

subnational_area: Dominican Republic, Colombia and six additional Caribbean countries
document_title: Resilient Coasts in the Caribbean Sea
notes: Through Caribbean living laboratories, the project restores mangroves and coastal lagoons in the Dominican Republic and coral reefs in Colombia and combines scientific monitoring, community livelihoods and scalable finance to strengthen blue carbon and coastal resilience. It is a demonstration and restoration action, but public information provides no verified additional-removal quantity.
source: Stockholm Environment Institute / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Started 1 April 2024; scheduled through 30 September 2026

document_title: Offshore Kelp Cultivation as a Carbon Sink
notes: This four-year project uses a giant-kelp pilot and subsequent larger farm off Namibia to study kelp-carbon export, deep-sea deposition and dissolved-organic-carbon storage rates and provide field evidence on the actual sequestration capacity of offshore seaweed farming. It is primarily research and does not show that all farmed carbon becomes permanent storage.
source: Kelp Forest Foundation / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Project ran from 1 May 2022 to 31 May 2026

subnational_area: Participating coastal sites in Africa, the Americas, Europe and Oceania
document_title: Adopt a Marine Carbon Sink
notes: The project establishes participatory science groups and local observatories for environmental and biological monitoring, site clean-up and restoration planning in salt marshes, seagrass beds and other coastal sinks and promotes community participation and open data. It mainly creates monitoring and restoration readiness and is not completed restoration or quantified additional removal.
source: University of Oviedo / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade action listed for January 2026; activity period has ended

document_title: Blue Carbon as a Canadian Climate Change Solution: Modelling the Mitigation Potential of Kelp Under Future Climate Change Scenarios
notes: The completed project established national estimates of kelp distribution in Canada and modelled blue-carbon potential under future climate scenarios to quantify possible mitigation contributions. Its outputs are models and national assessment, not kelp-farm deployment or a crediting methodology.
source: University of Victoria / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project completed on 31 March 2025

subnational_area: Shared Canadian and United States coastal waters
document_title: Exploring the Intersection of Coastal Blue Carbon and Ocean Acidification: A Synthesis of Biogeochemical Processes, Coastal Management Strategies, Knowledge Gaps, and Future Research Opportunities
notes: The joint Canada–U.S. technical report synthesizes biogeochemical links among coastal blue-carbon ecosystems and ocean acidification, management strategies and knowledge gaps and proposes priorities for future joint research and decision support in shared waters. It is evidence assessment and scientific coordination and creates no credits, mandatory MRV or restoration duties.
source: Fisheries and Oceans Canada (DFO) / NOAA
status_note: Canadian Technical Report of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences 3730, published in 2025

document_title: Project Selections for FOA 2614: Carbon Management (Round 2)
notes: In the second round of U.S. Department of Energy FOA 2614 selections, Area of Interest 2F supported eight projects for research, conceptual design and field validation of abiotic marine CDR, including direct ocean capture, OAE, regenerable seawater sorbents, electrochemical removal and mineralization. The page also contains a non-marine direct-air-capture-to-methanol project, which is excluded from the ONCE classification. The decision funds R&D and does not authorize commercial deployment or demonstrate the listed capacities.
source: U.S. Department of Energy (DOE)
status_note: Round 2 selections announced on 9 August 2023; the official selection page does not report project-level closure dates

document_title: Three Research Infrastructures together: Carbon Uptake Southern Ocean
notes: TRICUSO integrates European research infrastructures to improve marine-carbon sensors and data flows on robotic floats, uncrewed surface vessels and citizen-science platforms in the Southern Ocean and assesses observation density, data quality and governance for global greenhouse-gas monitoring. It builds an ocean-carbon evidence chain and shared observing practice and does not implement sink enhancement or grant deployment permission.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2028

document_title: Deep-sea carbonates under pressure: mechanisms of dissolution and climate feedbacks
notes: Deep-C uses high-pressure reactors, sensors and imaging to study deep-sea calcium-carbonate dissolution and its implications for ocean acidification, CO2 neutralization and global biogeochemical models. It is fundamental mechanism and modelling research, not marine mineralization engineering or OAE and does not authorize field deployment.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: ERC project active from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029

subnational_area: Deep North Atlantic and global deep ocean
document_title: NEutRally buoyant ParticlEs In the DEep Sea: turnover, origin and global impact on the marine carbon cycle
notes: NEREIDES studies the composition, sources, turnover and associated microbial activity of sinking and non-sinking particulate organic matter in the deep ocean to explain unresolved carbon budgets after export from the surface. It is deep-ocean carbon-cycle and biological-pump research and does not implement biomass sinking or burial.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: ERC project active from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2029

subnational_area: Arctic and Antarctic coastal and ocean habitats
document_title: Polar Ocean Mitigation Potential
notes: POMP quantifies biological-carbon flows in emerging polar coastal and marine blue-carbon habitats from primary production through transformation, intermediate storage and long-term sequestration, using ecosystem models and remote sensing and studying conditions for national and international accounting. It provides assessment and policy briefs and is not an adopted methodology, crediting scheme or enhancement project.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028

subnational_area: European and global ocean observing systems
document_title: Enhancing Biogeochemical Essential Ocean Variables for European and Global Assessments
notes: BioGeoSea improves observation, field validation, model representation, indicators and data products for biogeochemical Essential Ocean Variables, focusing on acidification, deoxygenation, the biological carbon pump and greenhouse-gas fluxes and updating EOV requirements and technical specifications. It builds shared observation and quality standards but is not a carbon-credit MRV methodology and does not authorize negative-emissions projects.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 September 2025 to 28 February 2029

document_title: Ocean-ICU Improving Carbon Understanding
notes: OceanICU measures and models the ocean carbon sink, with emphasis on biological-pump processes involving higher-trophic-level behavior and the relationship between human pressures such as fisheries, energy and mineral extraction and ocean carbon storage, and develops tools for the IPCC, global stocktake and management. It is evidence and model development, not engineering deployment or crediting.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 November 2022 to 31 October 2027

document_title: Global and local impacts on Atlantic RHODOlith beds: Implications for estimates of blue CARbon ecosystem services
notes: RHODOCAR assessed photosynthesis, calcification, carbonate production, carbon fluxes and storage in Atlantic rhodolith beds and effects of climate change and local pressures on their natural blue-carbon-sink function to evaluate the evidence for mitigation policy. The completed project did not establish restoration, an accounting methodology or a crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Marie Skłodowska-Curie project ran from 1 June 2019 to 31 May 2021 and is closed

document_title: How do diazotrophs shape the ocean biological carbon pump? A global approach, from the single cell to the ecosystem
notes: HOPE studies how nitrogen-fixing organisms shape the marine biological carbon pump from cellular to ecosystem scales and supports understanding of global ocean carbon export and sequestration. It is fundamental science, not ocean fertilization, microalgae engineering or commercial sink-enhancement deployment.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: ERC project active from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2027

document_title: Carbon Cascades from Land to Ocean in the Anthropocene
notes: C-CASCADES studied the transport, transformation and ultimate fate of carbon across rivers, lakes, estuaries, coastal waters and the open ocean and incorporated land–ocean continuum fluxes into Earth-system models to reduce uncertainty in global and regional carbon budgets under human activity and climate change. The completed project was carbon-cycle and modelling research and did not implement land–sea coordinated negative-emissions engineering.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon 2020 project ran from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2018 and is closed

subnational_area: Tidal meander and coastal wetland environments
document_title: Coastal carbon release driven by tidal meander migration
notes: CarbTMM used physical experiments and process models to study coastal carbon release caused by tidal-meander migration, bank collapse and exposure of organic-rich sediments and to improve morphodynamic models of tidal networks. It identifies mechanisms of blue-carbon loss and sets no wetland-restoration area, negative-emissions quantity or engineering-deployment target.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Marie Skłodowska-Curie project active from 28 October 2024 to 27 October 2026

document_title: VM0033 Methodology for Tidal Wetland and Seagrass Restoration, v2.1
notes: Verra VM0033 v2.1 sets eligibility and procedures for quantifying net greenhouse-gas reductions and removals from tidal-wetland and seagrass restoration, principally through increased biomass and in-situ soil organic carbon, and addresses sea-level-rise and non-permanence risks. The methodology is active, but each project must demonstrate additionality and complete validation and verification; the methodology itself is not issued credits.
source: Verra — Verified Carbon Standard
status_note: Active since 4 September 2023; methodology update remains pending

document_title: Blue Carbon and Freshwater Wetlands Activity Requirements, v1.0
notes: Gold Standard's Blue Carbon and Freshwater Wetlands Activity Requirements v1.0 establish eligibility and general requirements for relevant activities under the GS4GG certification system. They must be used with specific impact-quantification methodologies and other rules. The page also notes ongoing Paris Agreement alignment updates, so the requirements do not automatically make every blue-carbon project or 2026 vintage compliant.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: Version 1.0 released on 22 August 2024; subject to the Gold Standard Paris Agreement alignment update

document_title: Sustainable Management of Mangroves, v1.0
notes: Gold Standard's Sustainable Management of Mangroves Methodology v1.0 provides a framework for quantifying and certifying greenhouse-gas benefits from mangrove activities. It is affected by Paris Agreement alignment updates and a revision process under NMC 151; the existence of the methodology does not mean a particular project has been verified or issued credits.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: Version 1.0 released on 22 August 2024; a separate revision proposal is under development

document_title: Risks and Capacities Guidelines for Blue Carbon and Freshwater Wetlands, v1.0
notes: Gold Standard's Blue Carbon and Freshwater Wetlands Risks and Capacities Guideline v1.0 supports assessment of implementation capacity, non-delivery or reversal of greenhouse-gas benefits and sustainable-development risks. It is a safeguards and risk-assessment framework, not a stand-alone accounting methodology or independent basis for credit eligibility.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: Version 1.0 released on 28 May 2025

document_title: NMC 40 – Afforestation and Harvesting of Off-Shore Kelp Forests and Other Macroalgae Ecosystems to Sequester Carbon and Boost Biodiversity
notes: NMC 40 proposes an accounting methodology for greenhouse-gas removals generated by cultivation of offshore algal forests and other macroalgal ecosystems and considers biodiversity co-benefits. It remains under methodology review, with consultation still to follow, and cannot yet be used to issue credits or claim verified seaweed enhancement.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: In development; methodology review status published on 11 June 2025, with consultation identified as the next step

document_title: NMC 151 – Sustainable Management of Mangroves
notes: NMC 151 proposes revision of the existing Sustainable Management of Mangroves v1.0 methodology. Its public status remains concept consideration, with methodology development still to follow; it is not an effective new version and does not alter existing project verification outcomes.
source: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
status_note: In development; concept consideration status published on 10 January 2025

country_or_region: East Asia and Southeast Asia / PEMSEA
document_title: PEMSEA Regional Blue Carbon Accounting Protocol
notes: At its 18th annual meeting in July 2026, PEMSEA approved a regional blue-carbon accounting protocol intended to use common approaches for accounting for CO2 uptake and storage in seagrass, mangrove and other blue-carbon ecosystems across East and Southeast Asia. It establishes a regional accounting and coordination basis, but official information does not show automatic conversion into binding national law or directly tradable credits.
source: Partnerships in Environmental Management for the Seas of East Asia (PEMSEA) / Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism, Japan
status_note: Approved at the 18th PEMSEA Annual Meeting held on 22–23 July 2026

document_title: Integrating Coastal Wetlands Data into Greenhouse Gas Inventories for Developing Countries: A New International Blue Carbon Initiative
notes: The international blue-carbon initiative led by the U.S. Department of State and NOAA developed tools, templates and technical assistance aligned with IPCC guidance to help developing countries incorporate coastal-wetland data into national greenhouse-gas inventories. The project ended in 2024 and mainly built accounting and capacity; it did not establish a carbon market or implement specific restoration.
source: United States Department of State and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade contribution implemented from 30 September 2020 to 30 September 2024

subnational_area: South Atlantic and Southern Ocean observing regions
document_title: Southern Ocean Carbon-Climate Observatory (SOCCO)
notes: South Africa's SOCCO uses ship-based and autonomous observing platforms, high-resolution models, machine learning and sensor innovation to study Southern Ocean carbon–climate processes and provide evidence for carbon uptake, removal and climate-resilience decisions. It is long-term observation and capacity building, not deployment authorization for a specific technology, and the project page does not quantify additional removals.
source: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), South Africa / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Long-term South African research initiative running from 2011 to 2035

subnational_area: Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area / Pearl River Estuary
document_title: GBA Smart Pearl River Estuary and Governance
notes: This UN Ocean Decade project uses Earth observation, remote sensing, drones and field surveys to monitor mangroves, estuaries and coastal ecosystems in the Pearl River Estuary, analyze hydrogeological processes, carbon sinks and degradation drivers, and develop indicators and models for coordinated shoreline–ecosystem evolution. It is observation, modelling and planning support rather than a decision to implement mangrove restoration or issue credits.
source: Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey, China Geological Survey / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Oslofjord Kelp Park
notes: Oslofjord Kelp Park is a kelp-cultivation and ecological-restoration demonstration in the Oslofjord targeting nutrient removal, CO2 fixation, biodiversity recovery and the blue bioeconomy, with research to quantify carbon-sink and other ecosystem services. It remains demonstration and performance validation; all carbon fixed by kelp cannot be treated as durable net removal or verified credits.
source: Bellona Foundation / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Nature-based pilot project active from 27 January 2026 to 11 May 2029

country_or_region: European Union and associated European seas
document_title: MPA Europe — Marine Protected Areas Europe
notes: The EU MPA Europe project mapped biodiversity, ecosystems and blue-carbon reservoirs across European seas and used spatial-priority models to propose a marine-protected-area network incorporating blue-carbon benefits. The project ended in July 2026 and supports marine spatial planning and decisions but does not directly designate protected areas, verify sinks or implement enhancement.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project ran from 1 January 2023 to 31 July 2026 and is listed as closed

subnational_area: African coastal landing beaches and marine areas
document_title: African Ocean Biodiversity Atlas
notes: This Ocean Decade project develops an African atlas of fisheries and marine biodiversity and includes a blue-carbon biodiversity action assembling data on mangroves, algae and seaweed to advise governments on marine protected areas and coastal management. It builds data and decision support and does not establish a uniform accounting methodology, credit-issuance system or restoration-area target.
source: Ocean Rock Base, Ghana / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2030

subnational_area: Coastal sites in Bahia, Pernambuco, Rio Grande do Norte and Maranhão
document_title: Contamination in Mangroves of Northeast Brazil
notes: The project surveyed pollution, water quality, biological communities, mangrove carbon and nitrogen stocks and greenhouse-gas emissions at twelve coastal sites in northeastern Brazil and conducted ecological and human-health risk assessments to support monitoring, restoration and coastal management in polluted estuaries. It ended in July 2026 and was risk and carbon-stock research, not completed mangrove sink enhancement.
source: Federal Rural University of Pernambuco / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project ran from 1 July 2023 to 10 July 2026

document_title: OceanPeak — The Global Ocean Carbon Cycle after Peak Emissions
notes: OceanPeak develops multi-resolution carbon-cycle models from coastal shelves to the open ocean and from the surface to the deep sea to predict changes in ocean CO2 uptake after emissions peak and quantify ventilation processes and storage timescales. The ERC project improves prediction of the natural ocean sink and is not an artificial ocean negative-emissions project or a crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: ERC project active from 1 May 2023 to 30 April 2028

document_title: ANTICS — Advancing Novel Imaging Technologies and Data Analyses to Understand Interior Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: ANTICS uses in-situ imaging, machine learning and new data analysis to study carbon-storage processes within the ocean and reduce uncertainty about transport and preservation of carbon in the ocean interior. It is fundamental research and observing-technology development and does not involve active material addition, engineering permits or credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: ERC project active from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2026

document_title: SEACOVERY — Biotechnological Tools for Assisting Seagrass Natural Recovery in the Mediterranean Sea
notes: SEACOVERY studies assisted natural-recovery techniques for Mediterranean Posidonia oceanica seagrass beds, including assisted gene flow, active preconditioning and ecological succession, to improve tolerance and resilience to environmental stress. It identifies seagrass carbon storage and mitigation as potential benefits but remains technology research without large-scale restoration or verified additional removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Marie Skłodowska-Curie project active from 1 January 2026 to 30 June 2028

document_title: REWRITE — Rewilding and Restoration of Intertidal Sediment Ecosystems for Carbon Sequestration
notes: REWRITE compares passive rewilding, active restoration, business-as-usual and non-intervention across ten demonstration sites to study carbon sequestration, climate adaptation and biodiversity in European intertidal soft-sediment ecosystems and co-design scale-up with stakeholders. It supports demonstrations and method development but has not established a uniform crediting method or equated demonstration effects with durable net removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2028

subnational_area: North and South Atlantic ship-of-opportunity observation lines
document_title: C-SCOPE in Action
notes: The project used commercial-vessel observation routes to measure ocean CO2 uptake capacity, connect BGC-Argo and sea-surface observations, and improve database interoperability and open ocean science. Completed at the end of 2025, it produced ocean-carbon observation and data infrastructure rather than sink enhancement or a crediting methodology.
source: BSH, GEOMAR, IOW, IDOS and UERJ / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project ran from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2025 and is completed

subnational_area: Indian Ocean and South Atlantic innovation ecosystem
document_title: SAILOR — South African Innovation Lab for Ocean-Climate Resilience
notes: South Africa's SAILOR innovation laboratory provides specialist mentoring, scientific validation, pilot development and financing pathways for ventures in marine CDR, ecological restoration and related areas such as sustainable aquaculture. It is innovation acceleration and demonstration support, not a government permit, credit-issuance mechanism or proven scaled-removal project.
source: Kinjani / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade innovation programme active from September 2025 to December 2030

subnational_area: Baltic Sea, Mediterranean Sea and North Sea
document_title: AQUASPECT — Advancing Quality Assessment of Spatial Patterns and Ecosystem Characteristics through Technological Advancement
notes: AQUASPECT uses digital twins, artificial intelligence, ecological models and new sensors to assess coastal phytoplankton, zooplankton and biogeochemical processes and observes carbon sequestration as a key ecosystem service. It supplies monitoring and modelling evidence and does not implement marine negative-emissions engineering or quantify tradable credits.
source: Sorbonne University / Sustainable Blue Economy Partnership / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: International research project active from January 2025 to December 2028

subnational_area: North Atlantic coastal ecosystems, fisheries and aquaculture communities
document_title: Ocean Mitigation Impacts to Ecosystems and People
notes: This Canada-led Ocean Decade project assesses benefits and risks of multiple marine-CDR activities at research and potential cumulative commercial scales for ecosystems, fisheries, aquaculture, Indigenous peoples and coastal users and uses participatory processes to support equitable governance. It is impact and social-feasibility research and approves no deployment.
source: Fisheries and Oceans Canada / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Ocean Decade project active from January 2026 to December 2029

subnational_area: Antarctic Circumpolar Current and Southern Ocean research platforms
document_title: Southern Ocean Microbiome and Geochemistry
notes: The project studies Southern Ocean microbial life and metabolism, bacteria–algae interactions, carbon dynamics and trace-element cycles and builds research platforms, tools and ecological indicators to explain biological-pump and dissolved-organic-carbon processes. It is carbon-cycle research and international capacity building and does not deploy ocean fertilization or another negative-emissions technique.
source: Shanghai Jiao Tong University / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: International Southern Ocean research project active from January 2026 to December 2032

document_title: ANTICS — Advancing In Situ Imaging to Study Carbon Storage
notes: ANTICS uses in-situ imaging, machine learning and particle-size-spectrum analysis to measure particle size, distribution and composition in the Atlantic and explain flux attenuation as organic matter moves to the deep ocean and its control on marine carbon storage. It is biological-carbon-pump observation and mechanism research, not biomass-sinking engineering or a deployment project.
source: National Oceanography Centre, United Kingdom / UN Ocean Decade
status_note: Atlantic research project active from October 2021 to September 2027

subnational_area: Selected coastal demonstration sites including Hokkaido and the Buzen Sea
document_title: 2026 Selection Results for Large-Scale Demonstration Projects for Blue Carbon and Other Sink Measures
notes: Japan's Ministry of the Environment selected five of seven proposals for large-scale blue-carbon demonstrations after expert review. The selected work covers offshore and multi-level macroalgae cultivation, expansion and restoration of seaweed beds, nutrient and material trials, underwater biomass measurement, carbon-uptake quantification and development of credit-related evaluation methods. This is a public funding and demonstration decision; it does not by itself verify net removals, issue carbon credits or authorize unrestricted commercial deployment.
source: Ministry of the Environment, Japan
status_note: Five blue-carbon demonstration projects selected on 5 June 2026

document_title: GEORGE — Next Generation Multiplatform Ocean Observing Technologies for Research Infrastructures
notes: The EU-funded GEORGE project develops and demonstrates a multi-platform observing system for the ocean carbon system, including autonomous sensors for seawater carbonate chemistry and air-sea CO2 fluxes. It also harmonizes technologies, methods, standard operating procedures, data handling and reporting across European research infrastructures. The project strengthens monitoring and methodological capacity; it is not an ocean-carbon-removal deployment project or a legally binding MRV standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Horizon Europe
status_note: Horizon Europe project active from 1 January 2023 to 30 June 2027

document_title: Global Subseafloor Ecosystem and Sustainability (GSES)
notes: The UN Ocean Decade GSES programme investigates subseafloor microbial life, organic-carbon reservoirs, carbon dynamics and the transition from rapid upper-ocean cycling to long-term sequestration in the lithosphere. It coordinates global research and capacity building and develops international protocols, investigation platforms, monitoring tools and ecological indices. The programme builds evidence and governance capacity rather than authorizing geological storage or claiming quantified carbon removal.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Shanghai Jiao Tong University
status_note: UN Ocean Decade programme active from 1 January 2024 to 31 December 2030

document_title: Crustal Ocean Biosphere Research Accelerator (COBRA)
notes: COBRA coordinates scientists, government experts, private institutions, policymakers and other stakeholders to address knowledge gaps concerning crustal-ocean ecosystems that may be affected by emerging uses including carbon sequestration. It studies ecosystem services and resilience, supports decision-making and trains future ocean-science and policy leaders. The project is an environmental and governance research platform; it does not grant permission for subseabed CO2 storage or establish storage accounting rules.
source: UNESCO-IOC Ocean Decade / Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences
status_note: UN Ocean Decade project active from 1 October 2021 to 1 October 2026

subnational_area: Mangroves in the Amazon and southern Brazil
document_title: TROPIC — Tracing Mangrove Outwelling Provenance with Isotopes of Carbon
notes: The EU-funded TROPIC project will use radiocarbon, lignin and related molecular analyses to determine the age and origin of carbon exported from mangroves in the Amazon and southern Brazil and to distinguish recent, labile material from older, more persistent carbon. It is designed to improve understanding of coastal carbon cycling and inform conservation and blue-carbon policy. The project is scheduled research and does not itself restore mangroves, certify permanence or issue credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Grant signed in March 2026; project scheduled from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2028

country_or_region: European Union / Island Southeast Asia and Western Pacific
document_title: m-CONNECT — Management of Coastal Networks Nurtured through Ecosystem Assessment, Collaboration and Technology
notes: The EU-funded m-CONNECT project will study ecological, biogeochemical and geomorphological connectivity among coral reefs, mangroves and seagrass meadows across island Southeast Asia and the western Pacific. With Indigenous Peoples and local communities, it will co-develop guidelines for conservation, restoration and ecosystem-service enhancement, including assessment of blue-carbon potential. The signed project has not yet started and does not establish verified removal quantities, mandatory restoration requirements or a carbon-crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Horizon Europe
status_note: Grant signed on 6 May 2026; project scheduled from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2030

subnational_area: Nine coastal pilot sites across the Baltic, Black, North, Atlantic and Mediterranean seas
document_title: REST-COAST — Large-Scale Restoration of Coastal Ecosystems through Rivers-to-Sea Connectivity
notes: The EU-funded REST-COAST project tested large-scale restoration approaches at nine coastal pilots, including wetlands and seagrass systems, to reduce climate risks, enhance biodiversity and increase blue carbon. It combined hands-on restoration, monitoring, financing and governance arrangements and developed scalable restoration and adaptation plans. The project is closed; its reported ecosystem benefits and blue-carbon gains are not equivalent to independently verified removal credits or a generally applicable restoration mandate.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Horizon 2020
status_note: Horizon 2020 project ran from 1 October 2021 to 31 May 2026 and is closed

document_title: MangC — The Impact of Global Warming on Soil Organic Matter Decay in World Mangroves
notes: The EU-funded MangC project used mesocosm experiments and isotopic analysis to quantify how warming affects organic-matter decay in mangrove soils and whether mangrove carbon stocks and sink capacity may weaken or become net CO2 sources. The completed project addressed carbon-cycle mechanisms and climate feedbacks. It did not implement mangrove restoration, quantify project-level additional removals or create a crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: EU-funded project ran from 15 September 2022 to 14 March 2025 and is closed

document_title: MarshFlux — Future Climate and Land-Use Effects on Greenhouse-Gas Fluxes and Microbial Processes in Salt Marshes
notes: The EU-funded MarshFlux project investigated how warming, sea-level rise, nutrient loading and other global-change drivers affect biogeochemical reaction rates, greenhouse-gas fluxes and the long-term cooling potential of salt marshes. Laboratory experiments were used to constrain future changes in carbon sequestration and methane and nitrous-oxide emissions. The completed project was mechanism and risk research, not a salt-marsh restoration programme or a source of verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Horizon 2020 project ran from 4 January 2020 to 3 January 2023 and is closed

subnational_area: Global mangrove distribution and ocean-export pathways
document_title: GLOMAC — Global-Scale Interactions between Mangrove Forests and Climate
notes: The EU-funded GLOMAC project examined global interactions between mangrove forests and climate, including coastal sediment carbon storage, export of mangrove-derived carbon to the ocean, population connectivity and climate-driven shifts in mangrove distribution. The completed project strengthened understanding of mangroves within linked terrestrial and marine carbon cycles. It did not undertake restoration, establish a national sink target or quantify creditable project removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Horizon 2020 project ran from 1 October 2020 to 30 September 2022 and is closed
